Feels like just another multiplayer FPS.
If you've played litterally any FPS in the last 3 years You've played one with most of what Siege has on offer. Yeah the tatical assemble your own foxhole thing is new I suppose but it pretty much boils down to the same formula every map. Which leads to the game feeling kinda samey, unlike Overwatch or TF2 where the maps all have unique and diverse layouts and designs that lead to each one feeling like its own little world. The many grey-brown-redish buildings of Siege re-use the same tired kill boxes and breaching points again and again.
Each individual match boils down to three "phases"
Phase one: Build your defenses/Probe the enemy defenses with rolling cameras.
Phase two: Who flinches first? it all boils down to who messes up faster
and lastly Phase three: Snowballing. Watch in awe as the game transforms almost instantly into a one sided slaughter. then get ready to do it all over again two more times.
The game is crying out for some alternate game modes because as it stands its pretty much nothing but team death match.
Each of the in game playable characters does at least feel some what unique but going with the games feel of drab realistic military shooting 'action' they kind of all blend into one another as just endless veriations of dudes and dudettes in armour. Plus with the lack of dialog it gets even harder to tell them apart. (If I had a penny for every single time I've heard the same line repeated two/three times in one phase I'd be semi-rich)
The game's customization is pretty lackluster again thanks to the drab-military themes we can't have a lot of alternate armour skins (Unless your willing to pay out ragous micro-transactions)
Also the game has a veritable buffet of Micro-transactions and pointless DLC, season passes and other nonsense the venom of Ubisofts french cheese smelling claws are all over this game.
But for me the killing blow came right at the start.
U-Play. I hate hate hate hate hate hate hate hate hate hate hate hate hate hate most modern video game anti-piracy tech. Most of the time it just slows the game down and reduces performance, while eating up giggabytes of my limited hard drive space.
Rarely it does what it did to games like Batman Arkham Knight. Thankfully Siege is not another Arkham Knight. at least not at time of writing.
But what does♥♥♥♥♥♥me off is now I have another stupid pointless private single company digital app clogging up my hard drive. AND another user name and password to memorize even though its only for one game that I bought legitmately.
In short: Its just another military shooter. Stick to something like CS:GO if you want an active comunity or COD if you want consistant updates and new content every year or so.

Story = Interesting / pretty good
Gameplay = really good
Graphics = good (aside from cutscenes / dialoges)
Guidance = overwhelming to the point of confusion
Controls = pretty good
Voice acting = decent
Replay value = not really... once 100% completed, why bother?
Overall = Well worth the money, even at full price.
Sumary:  I haven't completed a game in quite a long time... and I've never once gotten 100% achievements unlocked for any game. But this game was compelling enough for me to keep going and actually get it 100% completed. I'll admit that it got a little frustrating / confusing towards the end and I ended up resorting to some outside guidance through steam discussions in order to figure out my next move, but I'm sure I could have eventually figured it out on my own if I had that kind of patience. The 3 endings for the game (not including the optional pre-mature exiting the cave ending) really helped keep me interested in re-loading the game to see the other endings, and of course, the other endings kept getting better and better. The voice acting was a bit weird in places though. Like the 3rd ending
her reaction was a little anti-climactic and didn't really feel like a realistic reaction. As far as the guidance goes... the game really tries to help you out throughout the entire game, it even gives you an interface of details for each species in the game which helps a lot, unfortunately, if you forget something task related, or make a big mistake (namely the explosive seeds when you first get them and ending related areas)... it's possible to end up being stuck in the game with no clue how to progress further since you can't get the cutscenes / dialogs to repeat, so make sure to read and listen very well the first time.
Overall, I really enjoyed the game. Highly recommended for those looking for something different than usual.

I have to admit I wasn't particularly hopeful that Waking Mars was going to turn out to be anything special, but at the time of writing (1.3 hours of game time) I have discovered (and if you know what the game is about, you'll realise thats a pun) that it is actually a bit of a hidden gem. It feels awesome exploring the caverns, identifying new species and figuring out what their weaknesses, diets and method of reporduction are. The drawn and animated species in the game look really awesome, and species from the same group have distinct visuals so you can tell they are related. Also, I didnt expect a game like this to have a story but it actually has quite a nice interesting one, and some of the artwork in the game is lovely.  It does, sadly get a little bit repetitive as when not discovering new species you are simply planting old ones in an attempt to beef up the biomass meter, to progress into the next area. Adding to that, due to the fact that the game is set on mars, everything looks fairly similar, red, orange and barren. While this is nice at first it starts to get a little boring, as you descend deeper into the caves it would be nice to see some different areas. Coming back to this review, I will admit I have completely lost the will to continue playing this game, it becomes very boring and repetitive over the course of the game.
+ Lifeforms
+ The story
- Repetitive
- Lack of Diversity for Landscape
Waking Mars has an interesting start, and is very interesting to begin with but while I love the art style and models for the lifeforms on mars, I generally would not recommend this game.

This is a third-viewing angle RPG with non-target play. It’s hard to newbie to play this category. But when you’ve acquainted with it and had a good control ability, I’m sure that you liked it. In general, this game has a good graphic and sound, low requirement for your PC and almost no lag. You can move through targets, destroy or jump over impediments, so you’ll never be trapped. However, navigation system is not good, and it made you move around. I think you should control your character to jump over impediments or take a short road when you’ve acquainted with maps.
Skill system is so various. It’s divided into 4 types:
-Basic Attack: no consume any types of energy, no cooldown, use by left-click.
-Combos: use chain of function keys, consume stamina and no cooldown.
-Active Skills: learn in Skill Master, consume mana and have cooldown.
-Divine Skill: depend on your class, consume Divine Gauge ( you have 3 Divine Gauges ), no cooldown. Gauge will be increase whenever you do damage or be damaged.
Because this various, it requires players must be proficient in controlling and using all of skills. If you have high controlling, using skills ability, you’ll be a nightmare in battlefield. Beside it, you must have plan for your skill points, because you have more skills at high level, but low skill points. And one thing about Active Skills: when you upgrade your skill to lvl3 and higher, you can be fail in upgrade skill and consume your skill point ineffectually.
Character’s Stats (depend on your class and you can’t change it):
STR: Physical attack power and the amount of weight you can carry.
DEX: Critical damge and critical hit rate.
VIT: Determines your maximum HP.
INT: Magic attack power.
MND: Determines your maximum MP.
Classes:
-Fighter: physical class, lowest basic range, highest STR and VIT so have highest based-physical damage and HP, can be a good tanker. Fighters have many knock-down skills so can tank many mobs although have lowest basic range.
-Slasher: physical class, average basic range, have many AoE combos, highest DEX and crit-increasing skill so have highest crit, can be a good killer in both PvP and PvE.
-Mage: magical class, highest basic range and based-magical damage, many Active Skills with high AoE and range. Although Mages have melee combo but slow animation with less knock-down combos so melee is a weakness of Mages. Mages usually play hit and run.When Mages have tanker in party, Mages can deal a huge amount of damage.
-Priest: hybrid class, average basic range, all stats are average too, many skills to damage to targets who are knocked-down. Priests have greater physical damage than Mages and greater magical damage than Fighters and Slashers. Equipments for Priests have highest physical def, magical resistance and crit resistance and Priest is the unique class who has heal. So Priests are very important in a party, and can be a formidable enemy in a PvP battle.
I see many players got a trouble when they killed boss at map. I've played all 4 classes but I've got no trouble when I killed boss. You should play hit and run, observer boss's animation. And then, you move to left, right or back boss's side to deal damage on boss.
If you want to show your controlling skill, creative thinking ability and your responsive, you can’t ignore this game.

Calling this a horror game wouldn't really do it justice.
SOMA's selling points are its atmosphere, its story and its immersion.
Frictional Games knocked the ball out of the park with their presentation. The world is beautiful and scary, unnerving and staggering. The best parts of this game are when you're not hiding from the monsters, but when the game lets you wonder around, immersing yourself in this incredible world they built.
SOMA forces you to take some moral decisions which really made me stop to think for a while before making up my mind on what I think is best. You don't often see this in video games – especially not in this genre – and it pushes the boundries of what can be achieved in the horror genre if not games in general.
The horror elements themself were what you'd expect – lots of hiding and avoiding, with the occaisional running from your life slapped in there for good measure. It's not an instant game over when the monsters find you either, instead they hurt you, causing your screen to distort. This distortion effect would stay until you'd heal at certain points scattered around the map.
The distortion is one of my biggest gripes of the game – it didn't feel necessary and even though there's a reason for it being in place, it just gave me a headache.
My second complaint isn't really a valid one when you think about it – the pacing.
In my own playthrough, I found myself getting stuck for long periods of time, not able to figure out what I was supposed to do. One the one hand this may have been a bit frustrating at times, but it did force me to look around more, check every door, which resulted in me discovering a lot about the universe the game sets itself in.
Overall this game is great, and I can only give it my full recommendation. It had my heart pounding at times, whilst simultaniously delivering an amazing narrative which was executed incredibly well.

I've finished this game more than a month ago.
But i still miss Soma.
I've searched for it in other games, but didn't find anything similar.
And probably i ever won't.
But still, i want more of it.
That's not because it's an unfinished game.
I'm perfectly satisfied with the ending, with the story, with everything that i've experienced.
It's just that i've loved it, maybe too much, and probably no amout of it could have satisfied the need.
I know that i'm gonna need to play it again, and again, just to savour more, and collect every nook and cranny that i can get my hands on.
And it's not because i'm a fan of all of the genres that someone can use to tag this game (horror, sci-fi, i will have to add a lot more, but i don't want to risk spoilering anything), it's about how this game put everything together and about what it accomplish.
Soma is A story, an interesting one.
A story that does not take you by the hand, as it does not need to guide you with markers, objectives, paths.
Still, it fills you with the urge and the desire to get around, play with it, know it deeply.
No side quest, no achievements, no extras: the core is all about you need, is all about you want.
A note aside: a special thanks goes to Frictional Games, Thomas Grip, their blog "In the game of madness", all their rant about interactive storytelling, 4-Layers and everything that had come out from all that brainstorming. This game is the living proof that you took the right direction, along with the Astronauts take on the subject with "The Vanishing of Ethan Carter". I'm sure that with time more and more people, even from other videogame genres, will follow your approach (and probably help you fix the missing points). In the meantime, thanks for everything

I had such high hopes of this game, based on the weight of positive reviews here and the fact that many of the games I like best  have an eastern European origin and setting.
I was sorely disappointed, for several reasons.
For most of the game, what you see on screen pulses in and out of focus, presumably to represent the illness of the player's character.  This, together with the movement of the character's head as he walks, made ME feel ill: it was like playing with a very severe hangover.  The head-moving thing is something I especially dislike: our brains work hard to eliminate this movement from our vision - only for game developers to add it back in!
The colour palette was turned right down: only in cut scenes was there any colour visible.  This may have had an artistic purpose, but for me it failed: the dinginess is monotonous and gratuitously depressing, in a way that (say) Stalker is not.
Add to that a weak story and undeveloped characters, and I found that I didn't have much incentive to complete the game.

This game is a blatant low-budget rip-off of Namco\'s \"Assault\" arcade game. And I\'m totally okay with that. \"Assault\" was incredibly fun, and so is this.
This game\'s control scheme is only \"unconventional\" if you\'ve never played an arcade twin-stick tank game. So, anybody who spent any time in an arcade between 1980 and 1995 will probably find that their muscle memory understands the control scheme before their conscious mind does.
All that\'s really missing from this game is the \"aerial launch pad\" mechanic from Assault, which was both a large-scale attack and a limited-range map peek. Nudge nudge, Daisy Maze.
\"Detailed graphics\" are also missing, but that\'s a testament to this type of game - the fundamental gameplay is more than enjoyable on its own merits, regardless of what arbitrary visual skin is draped over it. I feel that that\'s the true essence of \"retro\" games - the game-in-itself should be fun because of its basic structure, whether it\'s dressed in chunky pixels, 16-bit Mode-7, or HD DX12 photorealism. Or simulated ASCII text, whatever. The visuals represent the underlying game, and that\'s all they really need to do, if the game itself is solid.

"Milkmain of the Milky Way" is a indy creation that shines even when compared to more expensive narrative projects. The story is extremely creative and it's told with charming drawings, expressive pixel art character animations and dialogues in rhymes.
I was particularly impressed by the cinematic techniques used by the developer, who wisely mixed camera zooms, establishing shots and eventful cutscenes to masterfully convey the visual narrative.
Puzzles are easier in the first part of the game but become a little more complex in the latest stages. The logic of last puzzle felt a bit contorted to me, but that was probably because I forgot of a previous event, occurred in the first part of the game.
The length of the game is exactly what was needed to tell the story without dragging it. Being short is its strenght. I finished the game in a bit less than three hours because I enjoyed exploring every aspect of it but it's possible to finish it in about two hours, depending on how good you are at puzzle solving.
You'll be surprised by the unexpected turns that the story takes. I loved it and I recommend the game to all adventure game fans.

It looks like both good and bad reviews on here get thumbs down'd either way, no matter what they say. Nevertheless, I'll still add my two cents. I think the game is fun, but has some serious issues right now that customers need to be aware of before buying.
Launch was/is pretty bad, with the servers being down and up for the first few days, and off/on for some people even now. Jason's shift-grab combo (teleporting then grabbing the player almost instantly) can be frustrating to counselors. The price is pretty steep for the content, but I'm sure a sale should come around sometime soon. There are also some well-known game-breaking glitches:
- Counselors getting stuck in windows when hit while climbing through them
- Counselors getting stuck in hiding spots and being unable to be killed by Jason while stuck
- Car flipping over after randomly bouncing off of something (uncommon, but I have seen it once or twice)
- Counselors being able to get on top of some buildings/slide around in combat stance (haven't seen recently, might be patched)
- Party chat while in the main menu being choppy (not necessarily game breaking, but a frustrating issue still)
But there's also one last thing customers need to be aware of. This is an incredibly small team, and as a result, issues can take much longer than usual to be fixed.
This is all I can think of off the top of my head. As I have stated, this game has problems. Does that mean I don't think it's fun? No. Not at all. I recommend it, actually, on sale. It can be a blast, especially with friends.
tl;dr
I recommend you buy it on sale, price is a little steep. Has lots of issues (though they might be fixed soon). Takes a while for the small team to patch. Have friends that get it with you, or make friends on there and host custom matches. Maximum fun achieved.

I wrote the draft of this review shortly after playing
, but only now got around to publishing the review itself.
is a point-n-click adventure game about a fierce lady who will go to great lengths to protect her herd. Her determination is put to test when she receives an unexpected visit from above and embarks on a journey that will confront her with the cruelty of others and the emptiness of her own personal past.
Woven in rimes and delightfully pixelated graphics,
reads and plays like a cup of hot chocolate on a chilly night. Although the story can sometimes be more akin of the uncomfortable cold of not wearing enough jackets outside, the writing, the characters and the final questioning note of story surely feel like arriving back home and wrapping yourself up in your favorite blanky. If you fully embark in
, it unsettles you enough to take you out of your comfort zone, but doesn’t leave you desolate and freezing outside when it’s time to go home.
In essence, story-telling wise,
doesn’t disappoint; even tough it stumbles here and there when it comes to mechanics and puzzles, it doesn’t let that overshadow its deceivably simple plot.
is a game I recommend to anyone seeking high quality point-n-click adventures devoid of that – oftentimes despised – “old school” clunky feel. It’s a refreshing and modest take on an old genre, and is even more strongly recommended discounted at 20% or more, due to its brief playtime that I gather can be offensive to some.
To those with an already acquired palate for similar games, this one receives a strong recommendation, as
has mixed what it has learned from its predecessors with its own personal blend of the charming and the wistful.

This game is an absolute blast! I had never played any of the Sniper Elites before so I didn't know what to think at first, but after playing for a few hours, I was instantly hooked!
Pros:
-Controls are pretty good. Aiming through your scope gets more and more realistic the higher difficulty you are.
-Graphics are nice and there isn't much for glitching at all.
-Story was a tad bit short but it made up for it with decent amounts of difficulty throughout the game.
-Weapons are easy to use and don't feel clunky when you're walking around with them. Aiming either through your scope or by hip is pretty easy to manouver.
Cons:
-There is no system at all when it comes to customizing your loadout. Before each main story mission, you have the option of changing which guns you want to use but that's about it.
-No quick-save option unlike SE 3 which would have been kind of nice.
-When sneaking up on an enemy, there is no option, as far as I know, to perform any type of sneak-kill using a knife or whatnot which would have been nice too. You tend to waste a lot of bullets, especially with the dumb Welrod being it has the accuracy of a spud-gun...
-Not much for options when it comes to silenced weapons, which I know is somewhat understandable due to the time frame of the story, but only having a Welrod as a silenced gun is like infiltrating Nazi Germany with a very innacurate toy pellet gun. It literally takes one shot to each part of the Kraut body just to succesfully kill an enemy with that stupid gun...
-Noise cover-ups are somewhat nice in the game but you seldom come across one.
All-in-all it is a pretty good game, but it is one that would most likely be best when on sale.

This review will include both the main-game and the Foxtales--rather one story--DLC. Considering at the moment there is a bundle deal for both items and the soundtrack, I would recommend getting that offer if the game does interest you.
There are plenty of outlets that have gone into great detail on the shortcomings of this game. Namely, the gameplay. I don't really think I can say anything else than this game is a platformer: You jump, you solve simple puzzles with either the environment (mostly spirit guides) or some sort of tool (the projectile or a box or something).
I have heard from people like Total Biscuit that the KB&M controls are a pain to deal with, but I play these games with a controller all the time. Even on the controller, the gameplay can be stiff, especially when you are in a chase-sequence and you need to wind-up your projectile to knock an obstacle in-front of you under stress. You have to hold the aim-stick back, wait a second to charge it up, then fling the stick in the other direction to launch while running as fast as you can.
Also, I played this game solo, and yes, the AI will get stuck or get itself killed regularly, though I have found the AI fares better in the main-game now (but the DLC has the same problem). So the local cooperative play is perhaps your best way of experiencing this game.
WIth those issues put forward, now let me try to entince you to want to play this game. The main thing this game does excell in is its aesthetic. Not only do the models of the protagonists, the tundra landscape and other animals look beautiful but the mythical spirits and other supernatural elements fit so perfectly that even the natural landscapes almost seem dreamlike. And throughout the game the environments keep you to want to move forward.
Despite how simple the puzzles are, the game does feel well-made for a simple coop platformer. Of course, not everything mechanical is flawless; bugs, glitches or the delay on the projectile are minor problems. But if you appreciate both the pace of a good 50 hour RPGs and the no-extra-fluff of a 2 to 4 hour title, then I think you'll enjoy the game regardless of its brief length.
Lastly, there is obviously a lot of devotion put into honoring the creators' heritage, and it shows through the story and the art-style. The best way I can recommend this game is to ask you to not think of this as another simple artsy platformer like Limbo or A Story of My Uncle; it's a game-adaptation of an ancient epic tale from another culture. Like something you'd read out of The Odyssey. You have a heroine relying on her own skills and her compainion, the Fox, to overcome the challenges of nature and to save her family and friends over the seflish interests in some people. That is at least how I see the game, an interactive epic tale--you might think otherwise.
The story isn't going to be groundbreaking to modern tastes, obviously, but the story they do have touches on timeless human nature themes: Altrustistic communities, the error in selfish pursuits, the afterlife within our natural world, supernatural forces, etc. I think the way the game handles telling these stories with only the narrator explaining what the protagonists are pursuing and thinking makes for a wonderful tale for adults. There are some dark tones in the story that makes it feel very mature, yet nothing is too graphic for kids if you want to play this game with a younger sibling or child, unless death is too morbid of a topic to handle.
As much as I appreciate being given cultural context in the game, such as the projectile weapon or the beliefs of the creators, I rather wished the commentary didn't feel so shoehorned. You are not forced to watch them, but every menu screen will remind you of any unseen cultural insights. And the cultural insights are the only collectables to be found. Some of these clips do a good job in explaining what some characters, like the Owl Man, mean/represent and what purpose do they serve. Others I thought were too preachy or trying too hard to make the culture sound more original when they were using the same themes found in other cultures.
Also, some of the subtly is lost through these sometimes blunt explainations, and sometimes these explainations are reaching beyond what was shown to the player. For example, the introduction of the Foxtales is of the fox chasing a mouse and the girl following along--this apparently is the devs showing that the two are disrespecting nature by playing with animals and not hunting them. Is this clear to the player? Not really, not until the very last cultural insight are you told that was the moral of the story. It doesn't ruin the experience, but it does stand out compared to other cutscenes that tell the lessons of the story through actions and gameplay.
Total playtime of the DLC with several deaths and all the cultural insight videos, 70 mins. I find it hard to recommend current players to buy this DLC at the current discounted price as the name of the DLC should have been "A Foxtale", unless the devs plan on making more side-stories with the two protagonists. A season-pass or some sort of bundle of these extra levels would be the best idea to purchase, if more are on the way. What you get with this DLC are three levels with new puzzle mechanics added in: there is a small boat, some spirit rocks and a new boss-fight. The puzzles are more complex, yet they're still very simple. It's a rather bittersweet bonus story.
No matter how much I have nitpicked at this game, and how there are legitimate issues with the gameplay, I still think I got my money's worth out of this game. Perhaps you might think the same if you give it a try.

I wish I had known going into it, though, that there are some puzzles throughout the game, and several back-to-back at the end of it, that require looking at a bright, flashing image in high-contrast colors for up to a few minutes to solve. Divine Souls F2P MMO Review by Dionysis Spinos (for
Time for another review guys! This time I chose to review a F2P game that was added to steam really recently and I found it pretty good in my opinion and really worth checking out! Divine Souls is a MMO game created by GamePrix and published by Supa Games. Divine Souls is not simply a MMO game it combines a lot of different game genres and aspects. There are RPG elements, strategy aspects, dungeons and a lot of other things that make Divine Souls a really unique indie MMO game!
Let’s start our review by the graphics. The graphics of the game are good in general, the game plays in all PCs without any issue but you shouldn’t expect amazing graphics or something like that…they are ok and can satisfy pretty much every taste and pc, so I would consider this a more positive than negative aspect of the game! As far as the music is concerned, the game has some really good and satisfying music and background sounds that makes the game more attractive to the players but unfortunately I cannot say the same thing about the voice acting. The voice acting in this game is really mediocre and sometimes annoying. As far as the game itself is concerned, it features 4 characters/classes Fighter, Slasher, Mage, and Priest. Each character has a really unique set of skills and weapons. Also, I shouldn’t forget to mention that weapons have different rarities like every MMO which is another aspect I generally love in MMO games.
What other things I liked you will ask me! I liked in this game the fact that the quests are pretty match everywhere…so there is no way to get bored in the game. Also, the quests are really generous in rewards too and most of them have some hard bosses to find. Furthermore, the game features a really well designed crafting aspect…that will really help you during your journeys on the Divine Souls World! Other aspects that I generally liked in this game is the main city and all the worlds/places design. I should also mention the fact that the game features guilds, party system and some really detailed with videos tutorials and beginning quests that I found really helpful and fun!
Last but not least, I totally recommend this game to everyone, I liked it, the community and the devs are really friendly and they are ALWAYS there to help you in any question or whatever you would like to ask. So why not try it out? It is F2P as well!
Verdict,
7,5/10

From the makers of the horror classic Amnesia: the dark descent,  SOMA takes a lot of cues and mechanics from Frictional Games other productions. The game is not a survival horror, but more of a "hide from the monster" experience.
While mechanically similar to Amnesia, the feel and theme of this game is drastically different. The game is set on a deep sea facility that has experienced some sort of disaster. It is up to the player to determine how they got there, and what has happened to the undersea station. I won't go into plot details, as this game should be played as blind and spoiler free as possible.
What I will say is that this game is special in that it explores the ideas of existance, artificial intelegence, and what defines something as alive. All of this is delivered in a well written, well voice acted, and surprisingly intelligent story that never comes accross as heavy handed. The most spine tingling momments come when there isn't a single monster on the screan, but from the realization of what is going on and what it means for the main character.  It is a facinating puzzle box of mystery and terror. A must play.

The fact this has mostly positive reviews makes me lose faith in everything. I'm all for having your opinion, but this is the only game I cannot see how anyone can be at all positive towards.
So the glaring issue from the offset is that the game handles like♥♥♥♥♥♥ When the constant feeling of wading through thick mud isn't nagging you, then the absolutely pointless stamina and need to crouch to pick up half the items will.
After 15 minutes I lost almost all hope for the game being remotely enjoyable, since the translation is very poor, both in spelling mistakes that I can overlook to simply abysmal writing, which I hope for the love of God is actually a translation issue and not the intended result. The game looks okay. Some of the sounds are okay (emphasis on some, half of them sound like they were ripped straight from a game from the 90's). But none of it saves what is an incredibly monotonous, boring, glitchy and simply put pointless experience.
From what I can gather from the positive reviews, people are praising the story and characters the most, in addition to the Soviet setting rather than a typical American one... Really? The story is non-existent for 98% of the game. I don't know my characters motivations for wanting to go to the city. It's never developed, nor is the world and the events that led it to become the wasteland it did. You can look at a few notes that go into minor details about the virus, but the foundations are so weak you never want to.
The idea that the shift from the stereotypical rugged, grizzled and tortured white guy from America is any different to rugged, grizzled and tortured white guy from Russia is at all special or interesting is mind-numbingly stupid. The protagonist isn't fleshed out even a smidge. The♥♥♥♥♥♥that comes out of his mouth is so uninteresting it makes me wish this "walking simulator" took a few tips from The Stanley Parable and let me off myself 2 minutes in.
The ending made me both groan and laugh at how embarrassing the attempt to tug at the players heart strings is. Essentially, you spend the game trying to get the city to get to your apartment to look at a ♥♥♥♥ing photo album. This in itself isn't I'm opposed to. Say the character was a Mad Max type and the world had gone to pot and the game did a good job establishing both of these things. I could believe that a man with nothing to live for would want one last look at his family before he decided to die. It's nothing grand, but it doesn't have to be. It merely sets the foundation for a good story to be told through the rest of the game.
35MM doesn't do this. Instead you get a flashback about a wife and kid you never hear about dying in a car crash to
I was in shock when I saw they did this. The only character to have any backstory was your "mate" as the game goes on calling him. It's said that he lives in pain of his past due to a car crash. This is the only time character development is even attempted and the game expoloits it for an enormously crappy twist.
I'm focused so much of the characters and story because the game is a walking simulator of sorts, in that you do loads of walking but unlike a lot of other games in the genre, it throws in puzzle and point and click elements in too, which make the game even more of a chore to play. When your game is so heavily reliant on something other than gameplay, you must ensure it's especially good. I don't play Gone Home or The Beginner's Guide for the thrill of holding down the W key. I play them because they have good stories with fleshed out characters and explore interesting themes in an engaging way.
35MM doesn't do this. Instead you wander around a faux-open world with invisible walls for hours with nothing to engage you at all. It occasionally throws abysmal gun combat at you for some reason which, like everything else, is boring.
I don't go out of my way to play bad games. The ratio of good to bad games I play is heavily weighted towards the former, and as such when a game like this - a game I had huge hopes for due to a unique premise and an evolving genre - comes around I'm left feeling like I've played the lowest of the low.
I don't know how much I spent on this, but I feel ripped off.

I've spent around an hour with ASCII Attack so far but wanted to get a review out for other potentially interested gamers.
This game has mechanics that are heavily influenced by an old school arcade game called Assault (see
.  In that arcade game you had two sticks which controlled each side of the tank individually, requiring some amount of dexterity and learning on the part of the gamer to be successful at it.
Thats the kind of game ASCII Attack is.  There isn't any hand holding, there are a few screens explaining how to move in the game, no tutorial, no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t, you just jump in and get owned because you aren't automatically amazing at a control mechanic you don't use every day (like WASD or something like that).
I think that's what I like about this game.  My dexterity is challenged more than most games do, because I have to think about the way my tank moves and how I move it more than other games do.  I find myself getting better as time goes on, so I think higher skill can be accomplished over time.  I tried the keyboard layout too, which was really hard to get used to, then all of the sudden it clicked and my brain was processing it.
I like the whimsical ASCII art approach to the game.  It's bare bones to be certain, but cute in its own way.  I'm old enough to remember old printer paper like this and what a pain it was to tear the edges off without ruining my homework.  ASCII art used to be one of the only ways to do simple art for BBS's back in the day (yeah I'm old) and its fun to see it animate in this game with the moving tank, turrets and explosions.
The music is pretty good, if a bit repetitious.  That's a mark of an old school arcade game too, I guess.  It's cool to see music DLC instead of hidden away levels though.
Overall I think ASCII Attack is a pretty fun little indie game, it can be a bit tough, but I like harder games and I like the lack of tutorial and hand holding, I'm so tired of that.  Priced at under $3.00 is great too, my Starbucks that came and went this morning cost more than this game did.

At it's core, this game is solid. There's a lot of variety of heroes to pick with their own kind of playstyles and combos, as well as items to customize your own personal fighter which you can earn gear through the online multiplayer, or purchasing it with steel, in game money you earn from doing daily orders as well as playing the game.
There is a single player (or invite a buddy for co-op!) which allows you to play nearly every hero throughout it's duration, and goes over the basics of them. It's not very long, but was still enjoyable for what it offered. Every story mission you complete, you're given a premium box which gives you gear for your selected hero. (I'd recommend saving them until you've hit reputation 1 or 2).
But you will be spending the majority of your time on this game playing multiplayer, against other players or bots. There's a variety of modes, Dominion (a 4v4 mode where your objectively focused and holding points), Elimination (a 4v4 mode where you have one life per round, for the best of 3 rounds), Skirmish (a 4v4 mode of mayhem of running around the map with your team, slaughtering anyone you can sink your weapon into), Brawl (a 2v2 mode almost like Elimination, just more inclosed) and Duels (1v1 fight of skill, or whoever just throws the other off a ledge first). The combat in the game is pretty unique, I think, and the more you play as your preferred hero, there is some skill involved. There are some classes that feel a little broken, and the developers are actively looking to balance heroes. It's just is taking a while...
Ubisoft has a gem in their hands with this game, but it will require some more polishing before it will truly shine. Personally, I enjoy it a lot. The errors with connectivity for me have not been so frequent as thay may sound for others. I can't speak for anyone else, but if you enjoy a game with a bit more depth to it's combat and aren't interested in running around with guns, I'd say give it a shot. Divine Souls offers a gameplay experience never seen before. It blends an action RPG and MOBA into one MMO! Everything from the dungeons to the wave defense mode to PvP are all played with the same combo-based direct controls. Plug in a gamepad to enjoy it like any console game – for free!
Choose from one of four individual classes, each with their own specialized weapon and role to play. Delve into dungeons to defeat bosses and progress the story, solo or with a party! Create a guild and engage in PvP against other guilds, and join in on the Battlefield! There are always new and exciting ways to enjoy Divine Souls.
- Standing Out in the Crowd
A  wave of free to play brawler games have made their way to market recently. Dungeon Fighter Online may have been the earliest, but it was quickly followed by Dragonica Online, Fists of Fu, and several other titles. While all of these games had more action oriented gamplay than the traditional MMORPG template offered, they seemed years behind in terms of graphics and technology. Well now Divine Souls rides to the rescue. Not only does it offer fun bash-and-dash stage progression, but the interface and visual presentation are up to date. Divine Souls uses a familiar fantasy setting (though it does have some steampunk elements), but the visual style is realistic rather than anime inspired or cartoony.
- Not So Many Souls
Divine Souls entered beta testing in July 2010 and makes use of Outspark’s new O+ launcher.  The game has a wide range of supported resolutions and graphic options which is surprising considering the relatively small client size of 1 GB. There is currently one official server, broken into two parts with each serving a different coast. Each coastal server has multiple channels and can be scaled up with additional channels as needed. Character creation is a bit less impressive. There are three classes to chose from, Mage, Slasher, and Fighter. The classes are gender locked, but there are three empty class slots which means additional classes are planned in future updates. Appearance customization is pretty bare. Players chose from a small selection of face and hair styles. A full color pallet is available for skin and hair color. The character designs themselves look realistic, I was particularly impressed by the knees on the female Mage. I don’t recall any other game ever attempting to make a knee look so realistic.
- Take Control
The game starts in a tutorial zone, but players can leave at any time by hitting escape and confirming. Divine Souls allows players to switch between two alternative control schemes by hitting F5 or F6. Keyboard shortcuts are available to navigate the interface, and even to interact with NPCs, but players can bring up the cursor by hitting the ‘alt’ key. The need to manually switch the cursor on and off can cause some confusion, but is necessary to maintain the third-person-shooter like gameplay in Divine Souls. There’s no auto attack here, instead players click on the left mouse button to perform standard attacks. A variety of other keys are also involved in combat such as the space bar (jump), and ‘E’ (grab/hold.) Hitting these keys in certain sequences leads to combo attacks. Players can view a list of the combos their class can perform by hitting ‘K.’ The combo list is reminiscent of fighting games like Street Fighter, players who can memorize them and properly utilize them will be much more effective in both PvE and PvP. Luckily, its entirely possible to progress by spamming the standard attack.
- Persistently Instanced
Divine Souls makes heavy use of instancing. Cities, camps, and other locals that stock quest NPCs and merchants make up the persistent world where players meet and greet. Portals are scattered across these locations that open up regional maps and allow players to enter the dungeons, or stages, in that area. There are dozens of stages available but players will find themselves repeating them many times. Quests help speed up the grind and offer a sense of progression, but the best way to stomach the repetition is to find other players to group with. The level requirement for each stage is displayed on the map, but each stage comes in three difficulty modes. Players must clear a dungeon on easy to unlock medium, and clear it again to unlock hard mode. The persistent city plus instanced game world model was first championed by Guild Wars but stage based MMORPGs like Lunia and Divine Souls have done a great job adopting it for their own purposes.
- AoE is Effective
The best part of Divine Souls is its gameplay. As soon as the game begins players will have a chance to try out the combat system by attacking a group of portly goblins. As mentioned earlier, attacks are performed by hitting the mouse buttons and certain keyboard keys. Players pan the camera simply by moving the mouse which gives the game a live-action feel often lacking in MMORPGs. Players won’t simply be trading blows in Divine Souls. Each attack must be aimed and enemy strikes can be dodged. The developers may of gone a little overboard on the hit radius of player attacks. Hitting multiple opponents with a single attack looks cool, but being able to knock down everything in front of and to the sides of you reduce with a single attack reduces the game’s difficulty considerably. Its not uncommon to go through some of the earlier stages on easy or medium without suffering more than a few glancing shots. The crazy AoE attacks definitely add to the ‘arcade’ feel, however. Even low level bosses require some strategy, and more evolved tactics and team work are required in the later stages. Fortunately, it doesn’t take long to clear a dungeon. Stages themselves are broken down into a series of rooms connected by portals, players must defeat all enemies in a room before moving on to the next. Loot mechanics are designed to keep the action rolling, players simply hit ‘R’ near gold or item drops to automatically pick them up.
- Combo Breaker!
While new player will spend most of their time playing solo or cooperatively through the game’s PvE content, Divine Souls also offers a lobby based PvP system. Cities have arena buildings which open up a lobby where players can join or create rooms. There are four PvP modes (Deathmatch, Survival, Capture the Flag, and Break Into), and each mode supports up to eight players. By default, PvP matches normalize the level differences between players. A similar system is used in games like LaTale and ensure that player skill rather than time spent grinding determine the outcome of a battle. Players can turn off this feature and experience more uneven combat if they desire. Fighting against other players is much more difficult than fighting against the not so intelligent AI. Spamming the most simple combo won’t cut it. Players will have to learn multiple moves and when it is most appropriate to use each. Most player vs player bouts are team based, either 1v1, 2v2, 3v3, or 4v4. This means an element of teamwork is also required. Divine Souls keeps track of many PvP statistics such as wins, losses, rankings, and a player’s ‘PvP Point’ which serves as their rating. How well the PvP scene will develop remains to be seen, but Divine Souls is definitely the most exciting Outspark release since Fiesta Online!
Final Review:
Divine Souls is a fast paced action MMORPG that has great visuals and genuinely fun gameplay. Repeating instances can get frustrating, but Divine Souls makes it easy to switch between PvE and PvP to keeps things exciting. The game is pick up and play friendly, but the combo system requires dedication to master. If you don’t mind the heavy use of instancing, go try Divine Souls.

It looks like both good and bad reviews on here get thumbs down'd either way, no matter what they say. Nevertheless, I'll still add my two cents. I think the game is fun, but has some serious issues right now that customers need to be aware of before buying.
Launch was/is pretty bad, with the servers being down and up for the first few days, and off/on for some people even now. The price is pretty steep for the content, but I'm sure a sale should come around sometime soon. There are also some well-known game-breaking glitches:
- Counselors getting stuck in windows when hit while climbing through them
- Counselors getting stuck in hiding spots and being unable to be killed by Jason while stuck
- Car flipping over after randomly bouncing off of something (uncommon, but I have seen it once or twice)
- Counselors being able to get on top of some buildings/slide around in combat stance (haven't seen recently, might be patched)
- Party chat while in the main menu being choppy (not necessarily game breaking, but a frustrating issue still)
But there's also one last thing customers need to be aware of. This is an incredibly small team, and as a result, issues can take much longer than usual to be fixed.
This is all I can think of off the top of my head. As I have stated, this game has problems. Does that mean I don't think it's fun? No. Not at all. I recommend it, actually, on sale. It can be a blast, especially with friends.

Strictly speaking, this is just a simple two-hour pixel art adventure game written in rhyme, but the creator’s enthusiasm and the surprisingly charming and calming storyline make it stand out of its peers.
Sometimes it takes effort to find something noteworthy in the current sea of retro pixel art games, but Milkmaid of the Milky Way is one such item.
Of course, one can easy to skim past it, especially considering this is just a simple point ‘n’ click with a somewhat outlandish premise: a Norwegian milkmaid ends up on a spaceship of suspiciously human-like aliens and helps them to overthrow their despotic ruler.
The gameplay is also as simple as the art style. Although the levels are vast and sometimes it is tricky to navigate, there are no spots where we cannot get past with some walking around or simple trial and error.
Therefore, it is the atmosphere that carries this game. Maybe because of the rhyming narration style, but it feels like an all-age story equally created for children and adults. The result is a soothing mood that very few games these days can achieve, making this half-hidden gem of the Steam store shine probably even brighter.

First review out of the 50+ game titles I have on steam.
While the game started off very buggy (like most games do at launch) the devs have worked tirelessly to bring us the game we have all been waiting for. Friday the 13th delivers on so many levels.
Most games will be you and 6 other counselors against a very minicing Jason. If you have EVER WATCED a Friday the 13th movie, then you pretty much know how it will play out. As a Counselor your job is to work with the others to find items to help you escape whether that be by car, boat, or calling the Cops. Jason is a supernatural Phenom and an unstoppable killer. He has more kills in his movies then either Freddy or Mike so expect to die... A lot (and it's pretty fun too).
Jason begins the game weak, however, the longer it takes you and your fellow counselors to work together to escape, the stronger he becomes, like in the movies, he slowly begins to add to his kill count and trust me it only grows from there. With each counselors death,  your chances of survival deminish (as it should). Jason has special abilities which can make him seem over powered but I win more games as a counselor then I do as Jason, of course this being if you are playing with anyone who has a decent amount of skill and knowledge of survival games.
Each counselor is unique and you need to play to their specific strengths. You also earn in game currency to unlock perks to boost your counselor or finishers to add some spice to your Jason (there are 8 playable, 9 if you donated). If you think you are going to take Jason 1v1, wrong! I promise everyone else is going to point at your dead body as they run by and call you an ******* (insert your favorite diss here). The game's strength relies on numbers and co-op. The better you work together, the better chance of survival.
The game isn't complete, there will be a Single Player Story Mode along with a Single Player bot local game. More maps will come down the line but as of right now 3 are available. While visually this can become stagnant, starting positions and items are all randomized. I'm sure DLC will be on the horizon too but that is the trend of all modern games now, so really no need to ♥♥♥♥♥ here unless you haven't bought a PC game since 2005 or not into Multiplayer only games, which at this moment, is all it is until the later releases. So before you buy, make sure you are okay with that so the rest of us in game don't have to hear you whine.
Would I recommend this game in it's current state? You're damn skippy I would! The devs behind the game have been open with us from the begining. They are some of the most vocal devs I have ever seen (I was a GM for Funcom and helped release The Secret World and everyone that has played that knows how bad our launch was), and they appreciate all the feedback. It's a team of 6 guys so try and be a little understanding before you try and ♥♥♥♥♥ about how ♥♥♥♥♥♥ they are.
All in all, enjoy the game for what it is. If you're a counselor embrace that you are more than likely going to die, and die a lot, til you get a grasp of how the game plays. Even if you are the best survival horror player ever, unless you have a strong group of counselors, you're more than likely going to die. So have fun with it, I typically juke Jason for as long as I can while buying time for my fellow counselors to escape. Go out like a boss not a ♥♥♥♥♥. You can talk directly to Jason so have fun with him, once caught I always let him get a special kill as there are a ton of environmental kills he can pull off, and I have yet to die the same way twice.
Final Note - Counselors have a STAMINA Gauge and a SENSE OF FEAR. Just like in real life, you can't run forever, and if Jason was real, you would be scared ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ if he was behind you. When Jason is near, your stamina won't fill as fast and your screen will become darker and darker to emulate absolute TERROR. There is no FEAR Gauge at this time, but trust me you don't need one. You'll know when your counselor is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ their pants because you more than likely will be doing the same.
Now get out there and enjoy the mayhem. Make your deaths either meaningful or hilarious and enjoy delivering that final death blow to the counselor that has avoided you to the final moments of the game. Look forward to dying with all of you!

Awesome game! This masterpiece excels in every possible way. Apart from your convention gun blasting FPS, this game allows you to quad wield by adding 2 tendrils that you can use simultaneously with your guns. The gameplay is really refreshing and I typically liked the graphics style that uses cel-shading to give it a 2d-ish comical look.
The plot is rather straight forward but the way the story is presented with the incredible in-game voiced dialogue really captivates brings out each character.
The game is rather narrative where there are plenty of dialogs, but they are so well done you won't be bored. The level design are rather short although each of them stands out since they tend to have different settings. There are quite a variety of enemies to keep things interesting and I think the length of each level is just nice to keep players from getting bored.
The developers also added other game modes that you can play with friends with new characters and skills. I said friends because there are no one online anymore.
There are a couple of minor bugs which i encountered such as weapons dropped below ground and prevents you from picking up and the graphics jerk sometimes (during non-combat moment/close up with NPCs). The game also has almost zero replay value. This game had tonnes of potential. After each mission you head back to your mansion. And I think the game can use some upgrades apart from skills where you can manage back in the mansion.
Also, I have a 360 controller plugged into my PC. The game detected the controller and every button prompt are for the controller. I cannot find where to disable this so I was having quite a hard time figuring out the keys.
Many people are questioning why is there a DLC link in the library page but none was found in store. Unfortunately this game does not get the recognition it deserved. The developers really did a great job with the game but the sales did not hit their expection and further funding was pulled off including planned DLCs.
I was really hoping for a sequel of a prequel remake for PC. And this time it should get its well deserved recognition.

I have been playing Survarium since it's early days, only lately I've switched to its "Steam Edition".
If there is one thing I like the most about this game, that is it's atmosphere.
Fans of the S.T..A.L.K.E.R. series will definately find it attractive.
As a multiplayer, First Person Shooter it manages to be fun and even though there are few maps,
you cannot get easily bored. There is a constant progression with XP, Faction Reputation and Silver (in-game currency).
- Getting XP, helps you reach higher levels, on each new level you gain a skill point to spend on a "talent" tree.
- Faction Reputation is gained to reach new "faction ranks", which depending on the Faction you have chosen, will allow  you to buy different Armor / Weapons / etc.
- Finally, there is Silver gained, using it you can repair your gear (armor, weapon), replenish ammunition / grenades / first aid kits / etc. or even pay for Weapon / Armor upgrades.
The item upgrades are random attributes which cost money and "upgrade tokens" which can only be obtained randomly after each game or by dismantling another item. Also note that item upgrades paid with silver have a 50% probability of success but if paid with gold (micro transaction currency), they have 100% probability but still grant a random stat.
The item upgrade random stat can be from Health Regeneration, to Bleed Effect Reduction and the statistic amount given is also random (0.5% - 2.5% for example). If you receive an unwanted stat or a low number, you can pay with silver every 6 hours to attempt to get a better mod or with gold for instant and unlimited retries.
All in all, the game is fun and allows various play styles (close quarters combat, long range with snipers, etc).
It has a steep learning curve I might say and at the low levels/tiers of gear (not levels of character), there are possibly some hackers around to make your life miserable. As you progress and level up your gear, you will encounter less and less hackers but at the same time, better geared/experienced players which might seem to you as hackers...
It requires heavy "grind" to level up both your XP and Faction Reputation, at the same time you will gather silver and use it purchase new gear. It takes time but it is worth it.
I will end this review by saying this: if you want to play an easy multiplayer FPS that you can master and be good at in a few days, this game is not for you. This game, is mostly gear based which cannot be obtained easily/fast (unless you pay with real money).
Do I pay for gear or premium subscription? No.
Do I enjoy the game and plan to keep playing it? Yes.
Have I reached the top level / rank / tier? No.

Review of Single-Player Mode, as I have not touched any of Multiplayer or DLC.
You play as an American sniper in Germany during WW2. Your objectives will usually consist of reaching a vantage point, and sniping a high profile target, such as a general. A pretty generic, who-gives-a♥♥♥♥♥♥story, but that's not why I like this game.
It's a stealth-based, cover-based, 3rd person shooter. It seems that out of all of the weapons, only one weapon is suppressed; the short-range Welrod Pistol. I found that you'll have to sneak in close to effectively use it. Also, many maps have loud ambient noises(mortars, church bells, etc) that will mask your un-suppressed weapons' sounds. This makes timing key when firing your sniper rifle.
You get to carry 3 weapons; a sniper rifle, a sub-machine gun, and a handgun, as well as a handful of explosives. I find that the sub-machine guns are largely useless, due to the fact that the   firing spread is way too wide to be used effectively. I recommend only using a sub-machine gun in a last ditch effort. As for the explosives, you get grenades, trip mines, land mines, and dynamite. The dynamite I also found pretty useless, mainly because the only way to detonate dynamite, is to shoot it with your rifle. Everytime I started a mission, I removed the dynamite from my loadout, in favor of an extra trip mine/land mine.
The game's AI utilizes a "last-known location" system, similar to Splinter Cell: Conviction. Meaning that if you're seen by the enemy, you'll see a white outline of where you were last seen. You can use this to your advantage by setting up traps with your explosives, or lie in wait nearby and silently pick-off enemies using the Welrod.
What sets the sniping apart from most other shooting games, is the trajectory-based accuracy system. Meaning that bullets don't just go in a straight line until it hits a wall or an enemy; over longer distances, the bullet will begin to descend on a parabolic arc, so you may have to compensate for longer shots. The game makes this easier to deal with, when you empty your lungs before taking a shot. When you empty your lungs, a red diamond will appear, showing where the bullet will land. This is very helpful when you have to take a very long-range shot.
You can also tag enemies using your binoculars. It's a good habit of using your binoculars to scan an area to see if there are any enemies(especially enemy snipers) and tag & pick off before they have a chance to find you.
Sound also plays a large role in this game. I recommend turning on the subtitles in the settings menu, and paying attention for any chatter between enemy soldiers, footsteps, music from radios/music boxes. It can be helpful in giving you a heads up when entering a building or new area. You can also use sound to lure enemies into traps by throwing rocks. If a nearby enemy hears a rock that you tossed hitting the ground, he'll go inspect the noise, and he'll walk unsuspectingly into a trip mine you laid, or be in prime position to be picked off by you.
Overall, I enjoyed this game quite a bit. It was a bit on the short-side(I completed my first playthrough in about 12 hours), but I defintely see myself going back and replaying multiple times, simply because of how much I enjoyed setting traps and picking off enemy soldiers. I defnitely recommend getting the game.

Im not one to♥♥♥♥♥♥away money on video games so Im often looking for f2p games like unturned and warframe and such.
For a free to play game it is very fun. Maps look amazing, mechanics are solid, gun play is rather nice, community is pretty solid too. But like every other game it has issues
Pros-
1-Beautiful map design. Maps are very though out, often multiple pathways to get from point A to B
2-Guns are rather comfy, have yet to run into anything clunky to aim and fire
3-has a pretty solid gear system, pros and cons to various types of armor, and EVERYTHING is upgradable
4-You are not stuck having to buy things both in game money or Irl money, you will often find items after matches like medkits,guns,clothes
5-Active community so match wait time is very low.
6-Not required to pay money to have any form of fun, game is 100% playable without spending a dime
Cons-
1-There are bought weapons, these weapons are usually stronger than base game weapons but fortunatly the bought guns are rather pointless and useless after level 6. you can get weapons just as good, if not better through earning them than through the irl money store.
2-It takes a higher end machine to really run this game well. yes you can fiddle with the setting and all but to really you still run a chance at fps drop and stuttery movement
3-there are a few cheaters but then again when isnt there in video games
4-from what I can tell updates are rather slow.
5-the penalty for leaving games or going afk is not strict enough (in my opinion) and so you will run into games where you might have 2-3 people afk.
6-the lower level youa are the more toxic the players are oddly enough. but it seems to die down a lot after a few levels as it matches you up against people within a level range.
7-earning money can be rather slow at times, so progression is not the greatest. BUT you have a good chance at finding usable gear/consumable after each game so  suppose that makes up for it.
8-there ARE adds after each map but then again its a f2p game. there is bound to be a few adds here and there slutting for premium or to buy games with irl money
All in all its a fun game, *shrug* its free to play so its not like i can ♥♥♥♥♥ about money spent

Waking Mars is revolutionary. If I had to give it a genre, I would call it a Dynamic Puzzle Exploration Game. It is a 2D Platformer game with a very user-friendly item management system. It has definite influences from classic Nintendo games, combining the elements of exploration, isolation and atmosphere of Metroid with growing plants and food/nutrient management of Pikmin. Anyone who enjoys either of these should take a look at this game. Anyone who likes both (like myself) will probably sit down and play the entire game in one sitting. It is a rather short game, lasting anywhere from 5-12 hours, depending on how thorough you want to be. The 17 Steam Achievements are all very easy to get on your first playthrough if you give it effort.
SYNOPSIS: The basic premise of the game is this: you are an astronaut exploring a recently-discovered cave system on Mars. The only other characters are the Mars HQ woman and your environmental suit AI.
ZOA: As you enter the cave system, you discover living plant-like creatures, termed "Zoa" by your AI. These Zoa grow from different types of seeds planted in patches of fertile soil within the caves. You can carry a number of each type of seed at a time, saving them for later use.
RESEARCH: As you interact with the environment, your AI develops a research log. Once you have discovered all of the elements of a certain subject, you unlock a Steam achievement for that subject. Some of the elements are fairly straight-forward; others will take some serious thinking or random luck.
BIOMASS: Each Zoa in a chamber contributes to a Biomass counter. Once different levels of Biomass are reached, certain events occur. Some include barriers opening to new parts of the map, certain Zoa waking out of dormancy, etc.
SOUNDTRACK: The soundtrack is very ambient in nature and has an organic feel to it. It completes the atmospheric sense that the game presents well and does not distract from the action whatsoever.
ART: This game does not have your run-of-the-mill shooter 3D render graphics, as it is only a platformer. That doesn't mean that it has the pixelated style that has been popularized of late. Waking Mars has beautifully drawn background layers that fade in and out, giving the illusion of real depth. The art team did an impressive job with very original plant-form creature design. It is a bit on the minimalist side and gives a very realistic, tangible feel to alien Mars.
CONS: The only real downside to this game is the protagonist's personality. The AI is bright, happy and humorous. The HQ woman is funny at moments and believable the rest of the time. The main character is cold and sounds like he's talking in a combination of dictionary-speak and Medieval English. It is very awkward compared to the natural characters he talks to. This only really gets on your nerves during cutscenes, which you can skip (right mouse button).
I picked this game up on sale, but after playing it I'd say it's definitely worth the inexpensive standard price.
Final Score: 10/10

Do I recommend? Well in this games case I would but with qualifications.
F1 2014 is effectively an update to the 2013 game. The teams, drivers, tracks and rules are all updated to the 2014 season with the cars driving very differently from the 2013 versions. However I suspect given the earlier planned release of the 2015 edition (so we don't get the game with 3 races to go), that many features have been left out or just not complete.
There are clues throughout like the new bigger display steering wheels which are in fact copied and pasted between several teams.
The scenario mode, far from being improved from last year is truncated with no option to try the same scenario on a different difficulty.
The liveries on the cars are in some cases (McLaren) distant cousins of the real thing which will annoy anyone wanting accuracy. The graphics are an incremental increase nothing more.
The additional sting is what was removed, the classics last years seemed like a great beginning something that would be developed as the series continued but they are ripped completely from the franchise.
Personally I'm hoping this represents Codemasters shedding the limitations of the previous cycle to do something really special, with this release being a contractual obligation. I guess we will find out in 2015.
In the end can I recommend this? Well if, if you love F1 and want to recreate this season then yes. If you are just looking for some kind of F1 game, want value for money or have love for the days of Schumacher, Hill and Mansell then await the sale (or buy elsewhere) and get F1 2013.
If you already own F1 2013, well I hope my review has helped you decide.

From the makers of the horror classic Amnesia: the dark descent,  SOMA takes a lot of cues and mechanics from Frictional Games other productions. The game is not a survival horror, but more of a "hide from the monster" experience.
While mechanically similar to Amnesia, the feel and theme of this game is drastically different. The game is set on a deep sea facility that has experienced some sort of disaster. It is up to the player to determine how they got there, and what has happened to the undersea station. I won't go into plot details, as this game should be played as blind and spoiler free as possible.
What I will say is that this game is special in that it explores the ideas of existance, artificial intelegence, and what defines something as alive. All of this is delivered in a well written, well voice acted, and surprisingly intelligent story that never comes accross as heavy handed. The most spine tingling momments come when there isn't a single monster on the screan, but from the realization of what is going on and what it means for the main character.  It is a facinating puzzle box of mystery and terror. A must play.

Awesome game! This masterpiece excels in every possible way. Apart from your convention gun blasting FPS, this game allows you to quad wield by adding 2 tendrils that you can use simultaneously with your guns. The gameplay is really refreshing and I typically liked the graphics style that uses cel-shading to give it a 2d-ish comical look.
The plot is rather straight forward but the way the story is presented with the incredible in-game voiced dialogue really captivates brings out each character.
The game is rather narrative where there are plenty of dialogs, but they are so well done you won't be bored. The level design are rather short although each of them stands out since they tend to have different settings. There are quite a variety of enemies to keep things interesting and I think the length of each level is just nice to keep players from getting bored.
The developers also added other game modes that you can play with friends with new characters and skills. I said friends because there are no one online anymore.
There are a couple of minor bugs which i encountered such as weapons dropped below ground and prevents you from picking up and the graphics jerk sometimes (during non-combat moment/close up with NPCs). The game also has almost zero replay value. This game had tonnes of potential. After each mission you head back to your mansion. And I think the game can use some upgrades apart from skills where you can manage back in the mansion.
Also, I have a 360 controller plugged into my PC. The game detected the controller and every button prompt are for the controller. I cannot find where to disable this so I was having quite a hard time figuring out the keys.
Many people are questioning why is there a DLC link in the library page but none was found in store. Unfortunately this game does not get the recognition it deserved. The developers really did a great job with the game but the sales did not hit their expection and further funding was pulled off including planned DLCs.
I was really hoping for a sequel of a prequel remake for PC. And this time it should get its well deserved recognition.

People say it is a "hate or love" game, but do not go further with explanations. As I see it, the target audience of the game are the people who grew up in the Soviet Union, and thus who can relate to the environment, visual cues, and the cultural references. The westerners politely refer to it as an "alternative vision of the post-apocaliptic world". The younger Russians expect the constant stream of scares, explosions, and monsters -- just like it happens in any other western game. The target audience of the game likes the references to the dread of the countryside and poor people's living. It makes them recall about the heinous post-collapse 1990s, and allows them to re-live those years gone by when they were young, and had relatives and friends whom they held dear, and some of whom are not here anymore. I personally can relate to the ending of the game. This was the first game in the last 5 years and maybe 20 games which kept me awake until the early morning until I finished it. I bought it at the "-70%" sale, but it is worth to me the full price.

10/10. Perhaps one of the most aesthetically and intellectually stunning games I've ever played. If you take the clean, elegant design of Portal 2's puzzles, pair that with the level of personal engagement as seen with Bastion's narration, add a dash of Hitchhiker's Guide's humor, and throw it all together in a platformer you'll get Thomas Was Alone. The Darkness II is a sequel to the game The Darkness, where you play as Jackie Estecado, a key member of a mafia who is possessed by an evil entity that refers to itself as ''The Darkness'', which gives him a variety of powerful actions. The goal of the game is to retrieve your girlfriend Jenny, who has been trapped within the Darkness' realm.
To prevent any misunderstandings: this is in no way a horror game; the genre is action.
PROS:
+ Awesome action and combat
+ Upgradable tiers and multiple special execution attacks
+ Good variety of weaponry
+ The graphics are as light as they are good
+ Weapons feel and sound very satisfying
CONS:
- Relatively short gameplay for its price (5-6 hours)
- Lipsync is a little off
Anyone looking for an awesome shooter/slasher (you are the one that slashes), get The Darkness II.
My rating: 8.5/10

This review in a nutshell? The Reject Demon: Toko Chapter 0 is a kinetic visual novel that, while having some fairly important drawbacks, ends up offering something out of the ordinary for the genre and may be worth pursuing in that regard.
To begin, we'll go with some pros. In contrast to a lot of visual novels with convoluted storylines and serious tones, this one has a writing style that's very poppy and light on the tongue. This may be a direct consequence of the plot style, which is one of the main reasons I like this game. To sum it up, it feels less like a ponderous story and more like a (somewhat dorky) western-style comic book. The main characters are demons and angels and witches! Rock and roll is a demonic sex-magick! All the fights are based on music, with appropriate stings provided by the soundtrack! It comes off feeling goofy and loveable, which, together with some obvious tongue in cheek jokes about visual novels and anime characters in the script, make you feel like this was exactly what the design team wanted -- no world-shattering philosophies, just some light giggles. It's entertaining rather than illuminating.
The character design is something I both like and dislike; I give extra points for one of the main characters being drawn noticably larger than is the norm in the genre, and this not being used for comedy but simply a part of the character's design. Of course, everybody else is still ludicrously thin/amazingly bountiful in the chest department, but hey -- small steps, and an excuse can be made that most of those characters aren't actually human anyhow. There's also a strong lesbian romance theme going on, as might be gathered from other reviews; while this isn't exactly super romantic or developed (it's not that kind of story), it's there, treated as normal, and pretty enjoyable if you're into it. Still, the protagonist feels like a relative wallflower, who gets overpowered by funnier/more endearing characters like Nadia and Ginxhao.
Cons? Well, there's always another side of the coin to goofy and entertaining, which is that it sometimes feels like it's trying too hard to be cool in a very stereotypically adolescent way, and that pretty much nothing in this story is going to make you think; it's not very substantial in terms of themes. Or, as it turns out, in terms of content: expect an hour or so, and then you're done. That, I feel, will be the major sticking point for a lot of people who are used to VNs and wanted to try out something a little different -- for the price, there just isn't much there.
Ultimately, it boils down to a few questions: are there better visual novels than TRDT: C0? Undoubtedly yes. Are there better visual novels out there for free? Again, yes. But I need to stress that it
offering something a little different, and it is an entertaining little romp for how long it lasts. I feel like I should also point out that short =/= bad; time is precious and fewer people read extensively nowadays anyway, so it might be a good fit for somebody who's not overly interested in settling down and spending five hours getting invested in a story.
Final verdict: I wouldn't buy this at full price, not with the competition being what it is. But it may be worth a shot at sale price, if only to see if it's something you like. If I could half-recommend it, I would, but there are only thumbs up and thumbs down in this crazy world of ours, so I'll go with up since I personally enjoyed it. Just don't expect it to change your life.
