Waking Mars is an alien botany gardening sim, which is a string of words that instantly sold me on this game. You essentially create ecosystems by planting seeds that grow into plants, building "biomass" to unlock new areas and move forward. It's not so much a puzzle game for most of its run as it is a game of discovery, observing how different plants react to each other and trying to build a stable enviorment while only understanding part of what you're doing. Most of the game's delights are in that process of discovery. I've played a lot of novel games, and this one felt like it was exploring a new, fascinating gaming idea, where you model little ecosystems on the fly.
Unfortunately, it never goes very deep- completing most of the areas is effortless, and while the story leaves a tantalizing hook dangling for you to resolve, doing so apparently requires getting a perfect score in every area. Getting that score means messing with a lot of finicky parts that I thought was too frustrating to be worth the time. I wish the game went deeper by creating new puzzle areas and challenges, instead of forcing you to be a completionist. So I never finished this game, but the five hours or so I put into it were pretty rewarding. Bonus points for the amusing way your AI-assistent speaks: video games have a lot of "funny" talking robots nowadays, but this one is especially good.
You'll probably be seeing it a lot in indie bundles, which is where I got my copy. Pick it up if you have a few hours to spare for some inventive gaming.

I only recently got into this sim and I must say I am very impressed. The way this sim conveys the feeling of true flight is really very convincing. As an avid flight simmer (FSX, Prepar3d, Xplane, DCS, Falcon BMS, ...you get the picture) and RW professional pilot I think IMHO this sim has nailed it on all accounts : very realistic flight and damage modelling, deep "systems" modelling (as far as it goes for WWI), graphics are very nice for a DX9 engine, performance on my rig (4670k / GTX980Ti) is excellent (lots of options to tweak), and general immersiveness is top notch.
IMHO, I think compared to modern era aerial warfare, WW1 dogfights lend themselves better to PC flight simming with its inherent hardware limitations due to the relatively lower speeds and closer engagement ranges. It's the ideal platform to learn all about dogfight tactics and manoeuvres...
In short, for all flight sim and WW1 aviation enthusiasts looking for a realistic old-fashioned stick and rudder experience, this is simply a must have !

Reversed throttle controls?  WTF?  The throttle is apparently reveresed in these older planes.  Too weird for me to fly with a reversed throttle so it took me an hour of searching in the options menu for the throttle inverse checkbox (Options --> Responses --> All planes --> Current axis --> Engine control: throttle --> Inverse).  The menu itself is quite slow to respond to clicks.
Out of the gate, this game needs some configuring/learning.  If you are ok with that, then go for it.  The graphics are pretty descent for a 6-7 year old game and it's cool to fly these old planes.  The crashes are not bad either (the planes crack up on impact).  Oh, and I dropped a bomb by accident while sitting on the ground and the plane blew up...a portion of the wing went sailing through the air...nice effect!  Note to self...B is bomb, not brake.  Missions always start with the pilot staring down at the seat but a button on my HOTAS centers the pilots view easy enough.  And the FOV is a bit too narrow but there are buttons for zoom in and out.  The tutorial is impressive as it taught me things about flying that I didn't know (I'm by no means a seasoned veteran to flight sims...I honestly find them too difficult).
My recommendation to play this sim is not overwhelmingly strong but since there are so many negative reviews this is my attempt to bring the rating up a tad.  And hey, it's free to try.  If you end up liking it, then buy some DLC while they are discounted.  At the time of this review, all DLC is 66% off.

What you see is what you get with this game. And what you see is a constricting disappointment. Flower Shop: Summer In Fairbrook is a shallow, uninspired dating sim with a tacked on and unless farming simulator.
Steve is a dull, flat character with no chance to really gain any interesting traits. No matter what you do during your week, Steve stays the same. No new dialogue choices open up, no new events (You can go through each and ever event present in one play through, except for the ending events.)
Each of the romancable options are two-dimensional and boring. You have the standard affair of the tomboy, the delicate, the bookworm, and this games interpretation of friend from your old life. None of these characters stand out on their own or branch out from their preassigned and obvious roles. This game can't even do something interesting with the 4 simple, tried and true roles it uses.
The minigame of farming, which you would assume would be essential, is useless. The only thing you can do with the money you earn from it is buy more plants. There is nothing else that the money can be used for. And while the farming will inform your ending, it has no real measurable effect throughout the game. As the ONLY thing to do outside of simple interactions with the girls, you would hope it would be more interesting or even fun.
For diehard dating sim fans, this game offers nothing new, interesting, or even fun. For people jsut getting into the genre, avoid this game, it is representative of the worst in dating sims. This game is too fast to beat and lacks any real meat.
I would only recommend this game to dating sim enthusiasts looking for ANYTHING to play, regardless of quality.

Let me start with the following:
*  I have owned this game for years and downloaded the Steam version specifically to make this review.  No idea why it is rated so poorly.
*  You get 3 planes in the free edition.
*  Buying more planes is the way this game is marketed.  If you use steam you get these through DLC, if you use the Rise of Flight store you can buy individual planes.  However one you use one of the other, you can only use that method.  I don't know why they did it this way but they did.  However complaining that a free game doesn't have all the planes available, not sure why anyone sees that as a valid complaint.  The free version is basically a demo with 3 planes, two of which are good, the other if a Nieuport.
*  You will need at least a joystick, preferably with twist capability for rudder.
OK, so that out of the way, if you're still interested then let me say that of all the flight sims I've played, this felt the most like I was flying.  Maybe it's because the planes are slow, basically gliders with engines, but it is an experience.  When you pull out of a dive and your wings catch lift you feel it in the pit of your stomach, you can practically feel the lift.
For your first time out, I'd suggest going with the German Albatros D.Va (name seems familiar somehow), or if you are down to slap down money out the gate, the Albatros II.  Do a quick mission with no enemies and start on the ground.  Take off is as easy as putting the throttle to max, using your rudder to keep yourself going straight, and letting the plane gently take off.  In fact these planes want to rise, so you'll need some downward for on the stick to prevent yourself from stalling, just enough to stay level and gently glide up.  Do a few circles around your base then land anywhere that you won't run into a tree or a building.  Just lay off the throttle and gently come down.  The plane will bounce, it may break, whatever you don't have to pay for it and you'll be on the ground!
When you want a more advanced plane use the Spad (Spad XIII if free, Spad VII if you're paying).  You'll have to deal with engine management including radiator and fuel mix.  If you just want to shoot stuff then add a convoy to your instant flight and use the map/land recognition to find and destroy it.  Make sure you charge your guns first (you will need to charge them before they fire, no bullets, also they jam some times so keep the charge button handy on your stick).  When you are ready for air to air combat, set up one enemy, preferably something set to easy and of an earlier era.  Get used to manouvering.  Next thing you know you'll be buying a full HOTAS, rudder, and Track IR so you can really get into this sim.
It's easy enough, in the right planes (Albatrosses), that my friends who have barely any interest in flying find it fun (including girlfriends who don't play video games).  You'll also find many allied planes and some German planes to be unforgiving.  Hell some of them don't even fly right like the Dr.1 (Red Barrons triplane).  That thing takes a ton of rudder to manuever, but it's like a little floating deathball when you've got it down!  Then there are the giant 4 engine bombers that just barely get airborne, it's a challenge just getting off the ground, let alone making the bombing run!
I highly recomend this sim to anyone who likes flight sims.  I haven't even touched the hand crafted campaigns or the autogenerated ones.  There are more maps, seaplanes, a few Russian ones are around now, tons of aircraft modifications.  It is a shame to see this sim voted so low on Steam, it deserves better.  If you've made it this far, download the game and see for yourself.  After all it's free to try, and you can do a lot with the planes you're given (well two of them anyway).

I have to be fair about this game. So I try to play it simple. It is a dating sim or visual novel, whatever term you prefer. It isn't exactly bad - but it also isn't quite good either.
The story in short, you and your girlfriend break up at the start of a three month semester break. Your father is upset about you being a slothful , negligent and superficial way of life (what also was the reason your girlfriend was using to coerce you). So he puts you into his car and drives you to your uncle, who is a rural farmer. You have to cope with this, and your uncle ... you might fight against those things and befriend other girls, or you see that your dad, uncle and girlfriend might be right and develop some reason.
One of the things on visual novels is, that everything is about decissions and making it work out fine - in that way they are related to adventures of the type choose your own adventures - but this game has also a little twist. Your uncle is farmer, but his produce is restricted to fruits and vegetables and he's expecting you to also do some farmwork by giving your own plot of land a bountiful harvest (yeah, whatever) ... So you have to weed them, plant seeds and remove pests, water and in the end harvest them ... did I say that you also can muck your plants?
In reality this is truly backbreaking work, and you'll have to have a lot of patience over a long period of time (salads don't grow to harvestable size in three to five days) but you have to make concessions to get the game going. The money of your harvest goes into your own budget and this budget is used up to shop new seeds - you'll see where this is going? Yeah, at the end you'll have money for the things you farmed ... Fast growing plants guarantee a constant but low input in money, slow growing plants will cause a good earn in money (
)...
*sigh* In the end, your semester break comes to an end and you have accomplished: Nothing. Well you might have grown aquainted to one of the girls, worsened the relations to others and of course ... your family or the opposite of all this and grown a pro (hahahahaha) fruit and vegetable farmer with a lot of bucks at your own disposal.
And this is the thing with dating sims that do give me the creeps most of the time - on a pure fantastical setting all is fine and you can say, well this game at least doesn't give the pretension of being a sim - it is a story being told in which you are the protagonist and decide what is happening (I love the endless dungeon series from TSR back in the 70s and 80s, I also love Steve Jacksons and Ian Livingstones Fighting Fantasies) - but in a modern world setting a lot is going amiss, trying to be realistic doesn't help (hey it's a fricking dating sim) and too much fantasies also won't work (doh, look at those horsies *sigh*)
I grew up in a rural setting and to tell you the truth, this game has a far to simplicistic world view about a lot of things, but you have to start somewhere - this game got a E grade from me. Sure, it isn't all bad, but it also isn't all well and it has lost a lot of things - especially the "spoiled adolescent" role of the protagonist is a very painful stereotype.
I can't recomend this game, based on the gaming experience.

Story Spoilers:
Let me start this review by just saying that I guess I had different expectations for it. With that said, I think this game could use a lot of work if it were concerned with my thoughts/complaints on it. So to summarize what this game is about; You are a stereotypical slacker with low ambitions and a bit disrespectful. Your dad doesn't exactly get along with you, but figures your attitude needs changing so he drives you up to your older uncle's farm where you're expected to raise vegetables on a small plot of land. You get to drive into town within your first week of being there, where you'll meet 3/4 of the young women whom you can get to know better. Your uncle decides to go back to his normal schedule and lets you do with your week as you will. This leads you to several options for each day of the week; work more, visit the flower shop (Susana is here), visit the Library (Marian the Librarian is here), go for a jog (with Clara), stay at home (and talk to your ex-girlfriend Jillian), and relax. Choosing any of the options with the women will boost the tied "stat" that goes with it. These stats will reflect what you may or may not see when visiting the women.
Your days start with working in the plot of land you're given. You have to clear out squares filled with weeds to actually start planting anything. Plants take a few or several days to grow, depending on if you use fertilizer or not. Once they are grown you can sell it. The choices you have at the plot are; clear out weeds, plant something, using fertilizer, water plants, and clean up a plant. Any of these choices will take up 1 hour of your time, I think you have until noon to get things done in the morning before you go to whatever you chose to do that day. If you go to the flower shop you can choose to buy more seedlings to plant in your garden with the money you've gained from selling your full-grown plants (or not full-grown if you want to sell those early for some reason, I think that is an option, but I never chose to do that).
Okay, so I think I explained the garden part fairly thoroughly, let me just explain what I think was done wrong with it and why it's one of the complaints I have about the game. You grow stuff, you sell stuff, and you buy more seeds to grow and sell more stuff. You get money by doing this, and as far as I know that money had no impact on any other part of the game whatsoever. This gardening plot mechanic seemed like such wasted potential, and was a big disappointment to see. Plus the money you made from selling those vegetables would be less than you'd get working a part time job at minimum wage for the same amount of hours. Fertilizer cost $2, and sped up the growing process by 1 day, but takes away from your end profit and takes time to use.

I haven't finished yet, but I've seen plenty enough for a review.
Starting the game takes you to a menu screen that is in Russian. Easy enough to figure out where the options are and how to change the language to English. Game however doesn't have any English voices, so be sure to have subtitles on.
When you get to actually play, you'll look around and think that it looks pretty good and moving doesn't seem too bad either. Everything just seems to work.
You're then walking with your companion who happens to walk just slightly slower than you, forcing you to periodically wait for him. I saw him run for half a second but he immediatelly stopped when he saw that I noticed.
This game is all about walking. In an empty world. With little chitchat.
When they do talk, there sometimes isn't any audio.
There really isn't much to do while walking. You might explore some deserted houses for items, but you'll get frustrated when there is an invisible wall preventing you from going to a house just 2m away from you.
Did I mention walking? You do get to ride a traincar thingy, but that is boring as hell. They don't really talk and you just press w. Sometimes you get to press e to change tracks, but that's it.
Character animations are very sluggish. There is a fight that looks very amateurish and eventhough it's probably supposed to be "exiting" it's boring. At first I thought it was a cutscene, but in truth it was a quick time event.
I didn't notice because the notifications for each button you're supposed to press, was so small that it was easy to miss... Just slightly bigger than this font and no background, just the letter you're supposed to press.
Conversations are slow. One character speaks and it takes a while for another to answer.
At one point the game realises how boring it is and your companion turns a radio on.
Translation isn't very good either. Sometimes it's hard to understand what they're trying to say.
As it is, I wouldn't recommend getting it. The story progresses very slowly, the game is boring overal and you don't care about the characters at all.

35MM is an interesting little stroll in a post apocalyptic Russia. While dubbed a walking simulator, it is much more interactive than most, with moments of genuine tension, a bit of puzzles and combat, and movement options not usually seen in such games. It's perhaps better to think of it more along the lines of a mechanically lighter, bite-sized STALKER or Metro 2033 (albeit in a more mundane world).
The game is concise and fairly to the point. Most of my playtime came from exploration of everything I could, and getting a bit stuck on a few of the less-intuitve puzzles. But short does not necessarily mean bad - It's a small scale story, in a bleak world, with few words wasted. The world is fleshed out primarily through character actions and the atmosphere the game sets.
I wholly enjoyed 35MM. Don't expect a grand story or sophisticated gunplay, but if you're anything like me and just can't get enough of poking about in abandoned Russian countryside for a few hours, then this is the game for you.

I would recommend this game it has a fascinating storyline (if you spend time reading the documents that is), a scary atmosphere and makes you think about existential questions in a simple way. As soon as I started playing SOMA I couldn't stop the characters and the story makes you want to learn more and more about it.

You start off as a small, defenseless herbivore. Your job is to stay alive by avoiding carnivores while eating small plants and drinking water. You must work together with other herbivores in order to thrive. Eventually you will gain enough progression points (over time and by eating certain flowers) to become a larger creature. This will allow you to consume larger plants, defend against more predators, and/or outrun more predators.
You start off as a small, weak carnivore. You scavenge for small prey and left over meat on corpses in order to survive while also looking for water and fleeing larger predators. In order to hunt prey you can follow their footsteps they leave behind or sniff out their scent. The longer you survive the more progression points you gain, allowing you to become a larger, deadlier predator.
As the game states in the description "choose from three factions" this is the third faction which will soon be implemented. It will consist of two categories, modern humans and primitives. The modern humans will have survivors and mercenaries while the primitives will contain tribals and cannibals. If done correctly, humans could be an amazing game changer.
One of the best and worst features of this game in my opinion is the hatching system. Playing as a baby dinosaur is a lot of fun, it's a new challenge and adds to the environment when seeing baby dinosaurs. However, it is also a gamebreaker and my only con to the game. It can take someone 8 hours on a nonboosted server to become a Tyrannosaurus Rex but just a few moments to hatch into one. Sure they will have to defend against other creatures as they grow up but they will have their parents to protect them and will be stronger than most creatures after a little bit of growing (players do a good job at defending their babies too). Most survival servers I play on lately are roamed by packs (a lot of time most of the server) of Rexes and other apex carnivores which defeats the gameplay purpose of working your way up from the bottom. I do however love the mechanic and hope to see it improved upon in the future.
This game has
audio. Sounds play a huge role in this game, from the thundering footsteps to the echoing roars. Carnivores and herbivores have their own seperate chats, preventing them from talking in order to keep the realism. Whenever a player types in chat their dinosaur makes a roar which faintly echoes in the distance. These echoes create a realistic environment when a large group (herd) of players (dinosuars) are talking. On top of this amazing feature, players are given four callouts they can use in order to easily communicate with  other dinosaurs by pressing 1-4. These callouts are: Broadcast (loud roar), Friendly, Threaten, and Danger (help). These assist in creating an environment that sounds great. Make sure to have headphones!
The community right now might be one of the best parts. Herbivores can kill eachother, yet they
never do (a small herbivore tried attacking me once). They go out of their way to defend one another from the carnivores which makes for a great and realistic experience. Carnivores sometimes work together aswell which is a lot of fun, especially when you get a group of raptors.
The graphics for this game are great, but nothing special to be said at this point.
The animations are getting there, the main issue being with the head. Looking at water or behind you in certain directions causes your head to spaz out. The head seems mostly responsive to the camera until looking behind the dinosaur/ almost behind where it will look straight forward again. Eating and drinking animations are well done.
The developers have stated that the dinosaurs and their animations are currently unfinished.
Combat can be a little weird at times, but for the most part it's fun and balanced. Most dinosaurs inflict bleed damage, some do more bleed damage than others depending on bite damage and bite amount. This means if they try to run they will take more damage and also leave a trail of blood behind them which can easily be followed. Another combat feature in the game allows some of the raptors to pounce on other dinosaurs and attack as long as they don't lose stamina which can create some fun scenarios.
Overall I love this game and I hope the developers keep up the good work. The only mechanic that bothers me is the hatching system. I am excited for what will become of this game!
-In this review I explained the survival (progression) gamemode, there is also a "sandbox" mode which lets you freely play as any dinosaur you want.
-Progressing in survival mode can be extremely confusing for newbies and should probably be tweaked. Over time this issue becomes less problematic as you learn how the evolution tree flows.
-It seems they are taking steps to resolve the issue regarding nesting, an update will be released soon which will require both genders to create a nest.

I originally posted a review of this game unfinished due to what I thought were progress-breaking glitches and issues with the video viewer the program uses. I was contacted shortly after by a member of the team who assisted in showing me (incredibly politely!) that I forgot a fundamental system of the game and that there were no glitches. I have since finished the game and have watched 23/24 of the documentary videos.
I have changed my review to a recommendation, and will strike out any issues I once had with a write up on what has changed. I will also add some new insights I've found playing through to the end while erasing or touching up parts where I feel my originally negative review has since changed.
----------------------------------------
A fantastic game with an unbelievably charming story, an awesome art style, and a lot to teach. A truly special game that I cannot recommend enough.
Kisima Ingitchuna (what a beautiful name) is a story-based platformer that follows a young girl named Nuna and her fox to discover what has happened to her Alaskan village. A gorgeous canvas for a frustrating platformer that contians an incredible adventure.
Pros:
+ Visually gorgeous, with so much detail using a simple color palette.
+ An interesting, if not simple, story.
+ Narration in the native (Iñupiat) tongue throughout helps to flesh out the world even further.
+ The two player co-op option is a huge plus, and makes the game far more enjoyable.
+ The documentary pieces they have are incredibly well done. Not only do they teach so much about the people and their culture, they also feed back into the game's world through the stories they tell. Every part of nature, every struggle -- every piece that is placed into this game -- comes from the people's stories and their culture. What I would consider to be the highlight of the package.
+ STORY SPOILERS.
:)
Cons:
-
Turns out I had forgotten a fundamental system in the game. I have not found any issues like this at all.
-
Steam can sometimes not install the codec/viewer, and their support team had the issue resolved with a single email. I've added my thoughts on the videos to the Pros section.
- The controls handle incredibly loose. Using a gamepad, I had trouble making consistent jumps, which led to many deaths that felt unfair.
After completing this game and watching the documentary episodes, I cannot be happier with this game. Anyone who enjoys documentaries or thoughtful works will find much to love here. Easily recommended.

This game, to put it simply, is amazing. The animations are smooth, the storyline is enticing, and the combat, surprisingly, is quite interactive.
The ability to pick and choose whichever skills you want with no restrictions really allows you to create your OWN character. There is no "optimal" skill set, you just find the one that works for you. The game is extremley challenging on HARD mode, requiring players to strategize on every single fight; giving you a great feeling of satisfaction after clearing a room. Speaking of feelings, the gameplay intertwined with the storyline does an outstanding job at provoking feeling within you. Satisfaction, anger, happiness, confidence, sorrow; it's all there. Of course the game isn't complete, but I am sure that upoin completion the game will take players on an emotional rollercoaster, which will leave you saying "damn, that was a great game"
The developers constantly update their blog, so that players aren't waiting for new on new content for extended periods of time. They've even bothered to include special dialouge which will let you know when you have reach the end of the stable/ frontline beta (for the time being). And, of course, there are plenty of witty comments that you can sense took time and effort from the team.
Pros: Everything
Cons: Not complete yet
I'd have to say, aside from some very slight bugs (which I am sure they will fix) this game deserves a 10/10.
If you're looking for a game with classic graphics and modern mechanics, this is the game for you. Buy it. You will NOT regret it.

Waking Mars is an interesting concept.  At it's heart, it's a rather Metroid-esque exploration game.  Rather than focusing on combat, however, your goal is to explore and build an ecosystem within a large cave system on Mars.  While it's pretty simplistic, it does take some work to balance the flora and fauna in each room as certain ones will destroy others and can hurt you as well.
The game has a light story focused around the exploration which works well, though I wish the dialogue didn't force you to stop playing to listen to it.  It would be a lot nicer if it let you keep playing while the characters conversed.  It does have some nice hand-drawn character portraits though.  The characters themselves are pretty interesting, with the usual insulting AI and some decently acted humans.
Graphically, the game looks quite nice with the same hand-drawn feel, though animation quality is pretty poor.  Some may like it others may not.  One thing I really wish was done better is the music.  Good music could have added so much more atmosphere to the game.
Overall, it's a fun little game worth your time.  If you want to get the special ending though, you'll end up running back and forth all over the place for seeds which can get quite tedious.

FACT: 99% of all mobile games exist just to drain your wallet. I have found only three exceptions to this on my phone travels. A FMV game called "Tender Loving Care". A point and click game called "Yesterday". And this game, HITMAN GO.
Hitman GO is a minimalist puzzle game take on the complex hitman series.  It prides itself on boiling down all the complexness of bloodmoney into a simple yet challenging puzzle game (Which is better then it sounds trust me) Enough talk lets assasinate some ♥♥♥♥♥es and dive right in to HITMAN GO!
STORY
While the other Hitman Games had a rich story as the cherry on top of tight gameplay, HITMAN GO has no story and doesnt really need one. Your a hitman. Kill your way to the exit of each level. Sometimes the level exit is replaced with a random guy you need to kill. No Big Deal.
PRESENTATION
The graphics arent HYPEREALISTIC 1020P HD However. The minamalist board game style is not only really nice and easy on the eyes but also isnt distracting when you are trying to play. Even though the layout is simple you still feel like your sneaking around a airport or a suburban apartment complex. The game is usualy silent to help you concintrate, but the smoothe sounds of Ave Maria kick in in the levels where you kill your target. Which usualy calms you down from rage quitting.
GAMEPLAY
There are currently 5 chapters with two half chapters inspired by some of the other Hitman Games. All in All 91 levels with scaling difficulty. When you start out, its very simple. Get to the end of the level, dont get caught, attack gaurds from behind. But more and more gameplay elements get thrown in as you proceed such as everything from guns to gaurds with dogs and tazers. Mixing all these elements in with old things you learn is great at keeping you on your toes and makes for a great puzzle experience. There are also two alternate objectives for each level which requires you to finish the level whilst also doing something, like picking up a breifcase or killing everyone. Making a bit of replay-ability.
FREEMIUM ASPECTS
In the mobile version  the only micro transactions were to pay for walkthroughs or "hints" if you got stuck on a level. This was great because it encouraged the player to get better and find the solution themselves. In the steam version, there are no micro transactions at all, so cheat to your hearts content! WARNING IF YOU USE THE INGAME HINTS YOU WILL NOT GET A ACHIEVMENT!
Ranking: FULL PRICE BUY

Even though the story is mostly predictable, I did like the development of the characters. The main character going from a lazy brat to taking responsability and actually appreciating a girl for who she is. That said, there are some big downsides to this game which takes away the natural flow of the novel and instead feels like a huge grind if you want to experience the full game.
I dislike grindy Visual Novels and unfortunately this is one of them. You don't build up your love relationships by interacting with one girl through the story, instead you have to grind for secret points by doing different activites. That makes all the love relationships feel forced rather than naturally taking place. As an example, I thought the character Marian was most interesting, so I spent most of his vacation with her. The game ends without any acknowledgement of them liking each other at all and I get flowers from another girl instead. Reading the guides, if I spend less time with Marian, I can unlock the romantic ending with her. It seems very backwards to spend less time with someone you love to make them truly love you.
The huge downside of this game is the farming. Every single morning you are forced to the farm area. You can skip it if you want to, yet I would have prefered to not see it there at all. There seems to be no reward for actually farming. You can earn money, which you can only spend on to buy more seeds, so you can sell more vegetables. Yay? I would rather have seen that you could gift something to your potential love interest or save up money to take them someplace for a special event.

Flower Shop: Summer in Fairbrook feels like an early effort by the developer. The central charater is a boy named Steve who is shipped off to his uncle's farm by his father for making all D's in school and for being a selfish child with no ambitions and an attitude problem.
On the farm, Steve protests royally against having to do actual labor, but in order to try to have good relationships, you have to choose options that seem contrary to Steve's nature which takes some of the believability out of the situation. Steve is a jerk, but in order to make progress in the story, you need to not let Steve be a jerk.
The uncle seems to be an important character, but then he vanishes for 75% of the game. The girls Steve meets are all ends of what-the-hell. There is another boy named Jacob who is innocently attracted to one of the girls in the game, and you can watch his anxiety and care for her in every frame get ignored.
The farming mechanic is absolutely pointless. You can earn currency which is spent on more seeds to get more currency to do absolutely nothing more than buy more seeds. By the end of the game, I had saved more than $1000 and thought something neat would happen. Nope. No option to buy anything. No acknowledgement of my small fortune. You can earn lots of money FOR NO REASON, and this infuriated me.
So the game ends, and the one girl you were after never ended up liking you enough, and you don't really know what you could have done, but Gee Whiz, play through it all again and try harder, sport.

Evil genius can be described in a nutshell as bond villain simulator 2004. It's a base building game best compared to dungeon keeper, where your base is constantly under investigation by the world powers and if you can send them back home non the wiser about your operation then your "heat" level will drop. To this end you can create surface decoys, or train your minions in misdirection and distraction or even build a network of memory tamepering traps. You must also send your minions to various countries to conduct nefarious activity's but the interaction here is only through text and moving pieces around a world map. Still. many of the acts of evil are hilarious and well imagined. Evil genius is far from perfect, the AI is odd at times, the money earning aspect of the game is flawed, the traps don't always work perfectly and are redundant once the deathsquads start dropping in and it screams for more content but conceptually it has no peers and is a unique, stand alone game. It does base building very well, the AI has some great features like the minions spectating torture sessions and the writing is good. The typical bond troupes are such a fun idea to base a game around that the flaws can be generally overlooked and a good time can definitely be had.
-who hasn't wanted to design an evil lair inside an active volcano?
-the base building is great, the rooms look good, designing traps is fun and it's great decorating the place with the priceless stolen national treasures that enter your possession throughout the game
-the special minions are cool and good. Ivan is a jerk
-leaves you wanting more.
-just stealing all the money at the start makes the game much smoother and is a pretty good idea but this really screams about how annoying it is trying to get funds once the game starts rolling
-once the deathsquads come (and they will come) the intricate deathmaze you built is meaningless
-game could really use a sandbox mode or a scenario editor
-lots of waiting
Overall evil genius is a wonderful and characterful base builder with some unique twists to the formula and a fantastic design backing it up, so if you have ever wondered about the day to day of super spy villainy then you will probably have some fun with this one. Enjoyable, unique and engaging but imperfect.

It doesn't look like I've played a lot, but I know what I'm talking about. I've played before Z8 games, all the way back since OGPlanet (a lot of things happened - company transferred, people lost their accounts, used to be really popular. I've come back now that it's stable again, and since it's so so good).
This game is a North American adaptation of Korean Lost Saga. It has a unique hero purchasing system where you can buy heroes for periods of time - 2 hours, 10 hours, 30 hours, permanent, etc. You can use those heroes interchangeably in battle for combos. There are many game modes, but essentially you beat someone by making them lose their health/gear. Each hero has 4 gears that each have a special ability. You can replace some gear by purchasing gears in the shop, excluding weapons. The more you play, the higher rank you get, and the more heroes you unlock. In addition, you can level up heroes and upgrade them to make them stronger. It's a free game, so it's definitely worth playing. You start out with one permanent hero, and soon after you can get another 2 permanent heroes.
Some people call this a pay to win game, and some heroes OP. That's not true. This is a skill-based game. If you're good enough, with ANY hero, you can beat someone. Some heroes are more advantageous than others (premium, legendary heroes especially), but that doesn't necessarily mean you can't win. It's all about which hero suits your style of fighting. Others say that you HAVE to have an input hero to be able to stand a chance - not true either. There are so many playstyles around inputs that the people who say that don't know what theyre talking about. There are some people who've developed infinite combos with some heroes with the help of money and are OP, but Lost Saga is a team based game (mostly). Spending doesn't compensate for skill and teamwork.
The community isn't as big as it was back in OGPlanet, nor is it hacker free, but hackers are kicked as long as you enable auto kick for poor network. It's not a dead community - and it never will be, with the people who've dedicated so much time into this game. There are even tournaments in other countries where it's more popular.
Don't get turned off by some of the text glitches in tutorial and the guide/quests. Z8 is focusing on adding more heroes and events, not getting new players, unfortunately. This game has a unique combat system, it's free, it's easy going, and it's fun. This is the only game I cared enough to do a review for. Try it!

I liked the looting and looking around aspect of the game, but the health system felt sort of arbitrary given that there's only sparse instances of combat throughout. The combat itself is pretty clunky, there are some parts where you can die due to the firing mechanics not placing shots where you think they'd hit. You can heal with first aid kits, but they seem pretty much pointless unless you're in a pinch, since you'll usually have plenty of food, which also heals you but at smaller amounts.
There are 4 different endings as far as I can tell. I got (One of) the good ending(s). It wraps it up somewhat, and actually hits home when you realise what your character's goals were, even though it was a little predictable.
Overall, I enjoyed it. You have to have patience and a willingness to explore thoroughly if you're going to enjoy it fully, as the majority of the game is walking around and looting items, but overall it was an enjoyable game.

Imagine playing Mario Kart: you have a particular strategy, maybe not a very popular one, but it's yours nonetheless. Imagine while you are employing your strategy a Nintendo Dev logs in and uses a mechanic only available to devs to knock you from first place, second place, third place etc. Imagine playing Call of Duty, camping to get your sniper class leveled, and a Treyarch dev logs in with a special weapon that clears the entire Multiplayer Room. It's an inconceivable concept, isn't it? That you would purchase a game, spend time finding a playstyle, only to find it intercepted and controlled by the devs?
Welcome to The Isle. Welcome to a game where you can pour hours into progression of your particular dinosaur only to see it policed by the devs on any given day at their whim and fancy--- and, no I don't mean server admins, I literally mean the devs. Say you are a Rex, you find some food, you nest in a few of your friends, you are all laughing/having a good time and a dev just decides they don't want to see a Rex pack today. Well you can kiss those hours of progress goodbye as the dev will log in with over-powered, unavailable to the public, versions of dinosaurs to clear your progress. You want to play on a server with no rules, no holds barred? Doesn't matter. If that dev doesn't like you, doesn't like the resources you have amassed, doesn't like how many dinosaurs you have with you? Too bad for you! You can wave goodbye to the fun you were just having, and resign yourself to either starting over or giving up for the day.
The game itself? It can be fun, it can be stressful; you can run into friendly, wonderful people or you can run into your average run of the mill internet troll (which is the risk you take when opting to play a game with the general populace). The maps can be beautiful, they can also be glitchy and I could forgive the testing oversights and sometimes annoying, meaningless tweaks that are sometimes rolled out (it's still in it's test phase, afterall). I could forgive the annoyance of running into the unpleasantness that can sometimes be humankind (aka "killing on sight" for no rhyme or reason, corpse guarding etc.) because everyone who buys this game is entitled to make the experience what is fun for them even if that sometimes infringes on my progress. I could forgive all of those things, but the bottom line is: in any game, in any media, it is NOT up to the devs or the creators to police how I enjoy the product I have purchased as long as I am not using it to cause legitimate harm to others or exploiting it. If someone wants to make a mega-pack on a NO-RULES server then that's their right to do so, if someone wants to KOS on a KOS friendly server then that is their right to do so. It doesn't matter that I personally don't like mega-packs or KOSing or even Corpse Guarding, what matters is that devs should not be policing servers (especially those that do not belong to them), wiping progress from their userbase based on arbitrary impulse. I have seen it happen countless times, and each time makes me more and more tired of playing this game.
If you spend money on a product, you should be allowed to use that product without fear that the creators will crash through your window and destroy it. Period. I can't refund The Isle, but to those looking to buy I would say beware--- and certainly I will not be consuming any other games or potential DLC from these devs in the future.
EDIT NO. 1:
If you're really dismissing valid claims as salt you either do not understand what salt is or you are one of the fortunate to have never witnessed this. I do not think it's too much to ask that if I purchase a game I am not punished for playing it as it is presented to me. There is no enjoyment about being scared to log into a server for fear of being unjustly wiped; a person purchasing this game has every right to play as the dinosaur of their choice, not be fearful that a dev might come from above to kill them should they choose wrong dino on any given day. If the devs are concerned about balance then perhaps they should work on implementing balance in fair ways (eg. limit the eggs to one per hour) rather than punish the userbase for simply playing the game.
You would not expect an ARK dev to come destroy your base because you had amassed too many powerful dinos, you would not expect a Minecraft dev to wipe your server because they didn't like they way you were playing, and you shouldn't expect The Isle devs to come swooping in on Hypo Spinos just because 6 rexes were walking from point A to point B. I shouldn't have to play in fear, no one should, especially when no rules are being broken--- and if anyone comes in with "then maybe don't play as a rex or herbivore" or  "don't make herbivore packs" you are fundamentally missing the point. There shouldn't be an "if you don't like it play something else". I shouldn't HAVE to play as something else. I bought this game. I put my money and time into it. I should be able to play the dinosaur I damn well please just like anyone should. That's the point. Hard Stop.

The Darkness II (2012)
Great supernatural first-person shooter that continues the comic and original video game from 2007.
Having grinded the multiplayer achievements for Xbox 360 on the first game, it's not really a suprise I picked this up. At the price of $4.99 on sale who-knows-what-sale, it's definitely a bargain.
The game does a good job of filling in the blanks if you haven't played the first game in a while or at all. The first thing you can do is choose to watch "Previously on The Darkness." I chose to skip it and I still enjoyed the story having remembered the basics.
Another positive I want to add is that you can skip through the cutscents easily AND even skip each individual line when you have a conversation with somebody. I usually watch them but having the ability to skip is nice. And not Elder Scrolls-style where you skip and there's still a lot of dialogue to get through.
The shooting is solid as as the combat with The Darkness. I missed some of the "walk up and shoot the guys face off" animations from the first game but I was not disappointed with what was put in place of that. Weapon choices were great, a variety of each weapon type, new guns entirely, dual-wielding and even some guns that don't exist in this realm. Cool plot twists, the game definitely answered some questions from the first even if they were "What if" questions. It did leave as a cliffhanger but it's not one that leaves you mad at the game *cough Wolfenstein: The New Order cough*.
The skill-tree was cool, giving you some awesome abilities such as throwing a black hole that enemies can drop. The FX were top-notch so I was able to catch these effects with proper settings which leads me to its superb optimization.
Not many negatives, my only negative would be some of the moves with The Darkness but it's my preference. The game can set up some combos such as hitting an enemy in the air and then slamming him down, things like that. It's not a bad thing by any means but I'm used to shooting and not shooting while hitting enemies with my tenticles. It did take some getting used to but it's not your average shooter.
Keep it coming. Great game.
Oh, if you're into Faith No More, Mike Patton still does the voice of The Darkness.

The game appeals to me as it should apeal to any 90's kid the grew up watching everything about dinossaurs. With its animations, varietyof species, paisages and sounds it succeds in cashing in the nostalgia. But it mananges to be fun even after the nostalgia gets satisfied. The hunting is hard but intuitive, since you can rely only on the sounds and the logic of where would your prey or predator is. A feature that I really like is the camouflage and how easy it is for you to be ambushed or ambush someone, which gives to the game a constant tension, especially on closed jungle areas. In the other hand the game still needs a lot of work, especially in the servers stability (which is very annoying and gamebreaking sometimes), general bugs like getting stuck in holes or when you rest, the general hitbox of things but mostly a big revamp of the combat, which is the most lacking part of the game right now. I would like to see some ragdoll physics added, and some kind of grip system to hunt bigger dinos. There is also the fact of a much needed hit indication, both for getting hitted and hitting. But overall it's still a pretty nice game to play especially in group, even though some objectives besides survive are needed.
In general I would give this game a 7,5/10 with a potential to be much more.

You're probably looking at Survarium thinking, "Well, it has mixed reviews. But I'm a fan of the genre, I like the look of it. But I've heard some unsavory details about the gameplay."
Thats what I was thinking when I first downloaded Survarium. Like a lot of free games, people suggest you "Should download and try it" because you have nothing to lose, I mean, it's free. This title is no exception that rule, but you should know a few things prior to installation.
First of all, what is Survarium? Survarium is actually a team-based (although in the recent .30 update, which I have been waiting for, has an included deathmatch mode) FPS set in post-apocalyptic Russia. The maps vary drastically, from sprawling buildings to forests and wastelands. It is commonly likened to the S.T.A.L.K.E.R. games, but it does exist in it's own universe, despite the game using "anomalies", just like in S.T.A.L.K.E.R. This element flows into my next subject, which is basic gameplay. Players do all the things they do in your standard FPS. But the use of "anomalies" is something unique, as it gives players a buff or debuff, or so I've seen so far.
A few other FPS games do it, but in my opinion, Survarium hits the nail on the head with map hazards. The game's lack of map size is accented by various hazards and traps that you can fall into. It keeps the games fun and lively despite the fact that multiplayer isn't what its all ramped up to be.
Yes, the elephant in the room. Playing with other people. I have been lucky enough to be exposed to what cohesive multiplayer games can be, and Survarium doesn't rank on my list. Its one of those games where it has such minimal teamwork and tactics that you can't really tell if multiplayer is good or bad (in this case we have no choice, there are multiplayer matches and multiplayer matches only) or average. The closest I've come to working together was when I and another random guy camped a corridor to hold back a wave of baddies. I think I got a few kills before getting domed by a guy who, quite proudly, tea bagged me in his upper tier gear.
Yep, Survarium has considerable pay to win features. I always dislike describing pay to win games, as in my opinion, if you grind at something long enough, you can be just as good and geared as the other people who subscribe etc. I dislike people who hate a game for it's pay to win aspects, but I can understand their frustration. As stated above, you'll get "strate rekt son" plenty of times, and more often than not by a player who payed for his gear.
This is where my review can be really construed. Trust me, I hate pay to win games as much as the next guy. But you have to look past those
features, and review the
.
If you like the genre, check it out, its a lot of fun. If you like FPS games, I'd steer clear, as this slowly updating game has some less than stellar gunplay, and it can be a terror to run on average machines, as the game is unoptomized.
I rank 6/10, as it's fun and all, but it needs more. It can be buggy at times, and it can get old after you get owned enough. If there were to be created a "on the fence" option, I'd give this game that. But because I see the vodka bottle half full, I gave it a positive, as this game needs more reviews that are less focuses on money and more focused on gameplay and gunplay.

TLDR:
Really amazing competitive shooterwith plenty of characters for you to choose from (with more coming). Amazing gameplay, very much worth the money.
Basically...
There are a whole lot of characters to choose from, ones for defense and ones for offense. Offense has better scopes (Acog) for farther ranges (some defense operators have the acog). There are three gamemodes. You get paired with 4 other people (5 in a team), or you can squad up with your friends. You shoot and kill all enemies or play the objective.
Gameplay:
Bomb:
A multiplayer gamemode where defenders protect two bombs. Attackers need to plant a defuser in the same room as one of the bombs. If the defuser defuses the bomb, the attackers win, but if the defuser is disabled, the defenders win. If all attackers die, but the defuser was planted already, the game will still go on until the defenders disable the defuser or, if they run out of time to disable it, the attackers can still win.
Secure Area:
A multiplayer gamemode where defenders protect a room with a biohazard container. Attackers need to stay in the same room as the container for a certain amount of time to win, the defenders can stay in the same room and prevent the attackers from gaining any "time".
Hostage:
A multiplayer gamemode where attackers need to extract a hostage and the defenders need to prevent the attackers from taking back the hostage.
Terroris Hunt:
A solo or Co-op gamemode (up to 5 people). They can play the same gamemodes listed above, but with bots. They can also choose the difficulty- Normal, Hard, Realistic.
Situations:
Singleplayer content. (ish) I would classify it as tutorial gameplay. There are 10 Situations where the game teaches you how to play certain characters. After playing all 10, you will unlock an 11th, a situation that you can play with friends or randoms.
In casual, the objectives and the spawn place or random for all players.
In competitive, players can choose where they spawn (attackers) or where they want the objective (for defense only).
Ranking System:
Personally one of my favorite ranking systems because you retain your rank even when you done play ranked games, unlike other games *cough cough* Overwatch *cough cough*
Bronze4 B3 B2 B1 Silver4 S3 S2 S1 Gold4 G3 G2 G1 Platinum3 P2 P1 Diamond
Lowest ---------------------------------------------------------------> Highest
You play ten placement matches at the beginning of the season and you will be placed based on how well you do, the majority of players are in Silver and Gold.
Community:
I'm not sure about others, but from my experience, competitive has nicer people than casual. When I make a good play in competitive, the enemy players will congratulate me, but when I'm in casual and make a good play, the enemy team will cuss at me. Feels bad man. *keep in mind these are my experiences*
Graphics:
Graphics are great, there are some settings that will DEFINITELY tank your pc, but they might have fixed that by now.
All maps look very beautiful at all ULTRA and you can definitely tell they took their time making it.
Controls:
Basically what you would expect with any shooter, except ctrl is lay down, alt makes your character make less noise, but makes you move slower. You can ping so that your teammates know what you want them to do.
DLC:
For me, since I love shooters with destructible environments, the DLC was very worth it. ALL PLAYERS get all the maps that Ubi comes out with, but they dont get the operators for free.
Season pass holders get more xp, more renown (in game currency), and higher chance of getting loot boxes (called Alpha packs). They also get all of the DLC operators for free, without paying any in game currency. It may feel that getting money in game is hard and takes a lot of grinding, but when you start playing more, you realize that you get a LOT of renown really fast.
Overall...
An amazing game with a lot of content. Well worth the money. Get it with a few friends, your experience will be so much better, whether you play it really competitively or just mess around.
Pros:
- Great graphics
- Great community
- Plenty of content
- A lot of variety
- Not repetitive
- Competitive
Cons:
- Ubi doesnt always keep promises, they ended up not making a map they promised us
- Sometimes it glitches, but Ubi has done a pretty good job at getting rid of the really big bugs

First of all I must mention that i've played Always Remember Me which was also made by Winter Wolves and left a negative review. It's not that they are bad games, it's because they have some pointless aspects, they will force you to grind to get the different endings and they have a very short duration for $15+ games.
Flower Shop is a visual novel with a vegetable patch that you can manage in uncle Sam's farm. The story is good in my opinion, but to get the different endings, there is some grinding to be done. The art is fine i'd say and the music is good despite being repetitive.
On the good side, your choices affects the story and you have 5 possible different endings. As I said it's not a bad game, but there are too many things that makes no sense for me to recommend this game!
First of all, the farming part of the game: You have a plot of land that you can weed out, plant seeds and water them, then sell the product to make money... The catch? It's pointless! I've planted 5 plants at the start of the game and during the rest of the game I just choosed the option "Done working" and every single character told me that I was working hard and improving! I was also able to complete all 5 different endings without farming.
Also the price... $15? It took me 2 hours to get the 5 different endings (yes i've let the game opened for 1-1.5 hour to get cards) and after that, there is 0 replay value. I just can't understand why Winter Wolves sets their prices so high. It would be more logical to sell their games at a $5-8 price tag.
So overall, I believe the story was good and I enjoyed playing the game (alot more than Always Remember Me). But it's way too short and as I mentioned before, the farming part is useless. Feel free to get this game around $5 if you're into visual novels, as you might regret spending $15 for such a short game. I really wish in their future games they will fix those issues as their stories are quite good.

His character developing based upon choices you make.

Strange and enjoyable if you like searching for stuff. A "Jump in with no instructions" kind of game.
Three explorers have left on an expedition to an unknown land. As the player, you use your mysterious instruments to locate points of interest on the ever-changing topographical map. You are given no explanation of what any of your tools actually do, so it's up to you to figure out when and how to use each tool. As you locate these points of interest, you find clues to additional locations as well as diary entries from the explorers.
Experimenting with the various tools has a puzzle-solving quality, and there's an "a-ha" moment when you realize what you're supposed to be doing. Learning how the game works is the substance here. Using that knowledge to locate your objectives will take some time, but each tool has just enough application that you can exhaust its utility before it gets too grindy and repetitive.
My two criticisms:
At any rate, it's a fun diversion and a nice exploration game.

What don't seem to realize is that Rise of Flight on Steam is a demo. You get 3 planes and and access to the full game. The three planes you get are the German Albatross D.Va, the French SPAD XIII, and the Russian Nieuport 17 (which is actually French). The Albatross and SPAD are actually very good planes ( I personally am not a fan of the Nieuport, but hey you might like it). The lack of servers and players is because the game is from 2009, it was only added to Steam in 2013. If you enjoy WWI aviation, this sim is for you. This is a flight sim, not a game. Therefore, you are really going to want a joystick. If you play with mouse you're doing it wrong and it won't be particularly enjoyable.
However, the game still has an active community, even if it's small. The servers are fairly populated on weekends and weekdays at around 12-6PM EST. I recommend you go to Rise of Flight's website when buying aircract, as you can get the packs or buy individual planes. If you buy a two-seater, your friend could be your gunner if he didn't want to fly or vice versa.
This game gets negative reviews because people expect a COMPLETELY free flight sim. I don't see why, as they are getting 3 planes and the entire game for free. If you want a good singleplayer experience, play the career mode. If you want a good multiplayer experience, hop on the "New Wings Wargrounds" server when it has around 15 people on (it can have up to around 60 people on at once).
In conclusion, Rise of Flight is by far one of the best flight sims you can get your hands on. It takes you back to the early years of flight when dogfighting was a completely new thing. People need to understand that a game with as much content and depth as this is not going to be completely free. If money is really an issue, wait until planes and packs are on sale as you can get them for extremely cheap. Hope I helped.

I enjoy this game, I have since the OG version, and from what I hear there are a few common complaints about it that I need to address in the game's defence. The main complaints I've heard about LS on Steam are A) it is too "pay to win", B) the community is offputting, and C) the game forces you to do pvp.
(A)
I didn't transfer my account from when the game was still on OG so I had to start over and, just from experiencing the game from the start this time, I'd say it is much less "pay to win" than it was back in the OG days. If I remember correctly, back then you didn't get any perm hero to start with and just had to work with hires until you bought a perm. Now however, you get to choose from a dozen or so heros to pick as your first perm after you clear the tutorial stuff. Some people will say that to get a "good" hero you need to pay real money and while that is the case if you want a premium or any kind of perm hero I don't think the ones you're given to choose from initially are bad for any stage of the game if you use them right (I knew a friend back in OG LS that used death knight as their main all through their game). I also know from experience that some of these "good" heros you need to buy are also tricky to play as and, if they were included in the initial perm hero list, would just end up frusterating the people that chose that hero without knowledge of how to play it well. From what I've seen, most of the initial perm heros are fairly easy to play as off the bat.
I'm probably rambling and may have repeated myself once or twice, so I'll move on to
(B)
Ok, some people in a free online game are mean to you, so what? I challenge you to find one free to play online game where the majority of the people in the chat are just idiots trying to insult people. As a veteren of online gaming I have this to say: suck it up, ignore idiots, and enjoy the game. If you want to chat with nice, non-trolls all you need to do is make a public plaza, weed out the idiots that join, ask the kind players to be friends, and eventually you'll have a group of awesome people you can do crusade with or pvp with or whatever.
(C)
I've heard that because of the way the game is made, how the modes are set up, etc, the game pretty much makes you do pvp. This isn't true. I've played the game (Steam version) for about 3 hours now and haven't done one PvP match. I've fished in the plaza with friends, did crusade, and played on other cooperative modes and the game wasn't unenjoyable, laggy, boring, etc. There's even a prize list with some pretty nice rewards after forest or snow mode.

There was a time when I would have, and did frequently, recommend this game to everyone that played games. I was happy to play it, I was always excited when there was an update, and any time I encountered a problem, I was quick to find the bright side and even come back later. I held four accounts over the years and passes between companies and servers, and I had numerous heroes and gears, some rare and hard to get. Every little part of this game made me happy.
However, that has all come to a slow, painful, depressing stop. It started when I was first♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off by the original owners all but dropping the game on this side of the world. However, it passed. I brushed myself off with no troubles and simply resolved that it merely wasn't meant to be. I was even overjoyed when I heard that it was picked up again, and I was one of the first to sign up for the new one. Even having to make a completely new profile because of a foolish and easily rectifiable error by the company only gave me momentary pause. I was just happy to play again. But that's where it started to feel a little stale. Well, the game continued to fall down in the world's eyes, even to the point of the US server being excluded from an international tournament. That was when I first questioned how much I really loved this game. Still, I loved what it was, and I especially loved what it still had the potential to be. And when it lost this new carrier, I was mortified. I remember actually being depressed about it for a while. As you can imagine, this kind of embittered me to mmo's in general, and I fell out of a lot at the time. Well, it was with that still-bitter eye that I noticed the game had been passed off again. By this time, I was less than convinced that it would last, and so I entered in again with full intentions of not getting attached so I wouldn't care as much when it was inevitably abandoned again, but I always held out that hope that it wouldn't. Surprise surprise, it was axed again. Very unceremoniously this time, too. I'd given up on it by this point, so when I found out that the game had been put out on Steam, I was actually pleasantly surprised, and believed this meant it was for once here to stay. I jumped back in and played along, even enjoying all the new features and events.
And you know what? The game is still fun. It is unique and fun to play, and the concept is still pretty novel, as far as I'm concerned. I'd even agree that the pay to win model is fixable with hard work, dedication, and lots of effort.
So if I still like the game, why's this review negative? Simple:
The community is one of the most toxic I have ever experienced in my life, and the people in charge of the game do absolutely nothing about it. The best there is to deal with it is a block feature that does nothing before a match except keep you, and only you by the way, from reading anything they type, and a poorly made censor that messes up perfectly reasonable words because it looks for a sequence of letters instead of watching for the word itself. You can't even say Assassin. It comes out ******in. That is BS. So if you come across a person that is harassing the crap out of you? It's Half Life 2, but you get to watch people who are better at the game than you beat most of the monsters and drive you off of cliffs when you ride with them.
Really though, Synergy is a great game. It makes re-playing HL2 worth it, even if you've played it a lot in single-player. Inevitably it almost ends up like a speedrun contest, with all the players vying to be among the first four to the end of the level. Quite an entertaining challenge for someone who's familiar with the game already. I haven't seen many custom maps for the game, but from what I've seen there are some great ones. Plus, c'mon, it's HL2. Even if you're not doing as much as your teammates you can still enjoy being in a Half-Life game.
My only serious criticisms (aside from trusting total strangers to help you survive) are thus:
--Some levels aren't scaled up in difficulty, so the first few people to the scene get to kill everything and everyone else has to play catch-up.
--Healing and kill assists don't count for points on the scoreboard.
Though there aren't a lot of servers around for this game, there's usually someone on a server somewhere. Even if there's not, there's enough empty ones around that you can invite a few friends over.
Overall, I'd give Synergy an 8.5/10.

The gameplay itself was enjoyable, though towards the end the platforming becomes much more difficult and in some places downright tedious. There was a lot of trial and error involved. If you aren't a big fan of platformers (I'm not) you'll want a good deal of patience. Getting to see the story unfold is well worth it, and you'll want to unlock the videos for the learning experience.
I've read in a few places that there was some difficulty with the controls, but I had no trouble with them. Playing in single player I found it very easy to switch between the fox and the girl, and most of the difficulty with the platform came from poor timing and unexpected dangers.
I really hope to see more games like this one in the future.

*This review is just for the single player portion of the game which is all I played through and beat on the Normal Difficulty setting.
Pros:
+The aiming, iron lung, and killcam system when sniping feels very fluid, precise, and rewarding
+When the game takes a break from the stealth sections of each level to give you plenty of space and cover to take out multiple enemies bearing down on you with a sniper rifle, the gameplay feels fresh, fun, and intense
+Detailed level design in WW2 setting that does solid job of portraying blown out cities and battlefields (though it can all feel sorta samey and bland by the end of the campaign)
Cons:
-Enemy AI that have automatic weapons can be frustratingly overpowered and godlike accurate from unbelievablely long ranges when they spot you
-The stealth sections and gadgets were underdeveloped and tedious; only through trial and error of dying or replaying levels could you begin to guess where you should be setting up traps to defend your position as enemies could often flank you from several different directions
-Clunky Cover and Controls: 1) It's annoying running up to some sandbags or half blown up wall only to realize the game wouldn't let you take cover behind it 2) Taking damage while moving in/out of cover or crouching/proning in the middle of a fight felt was so slow/glitchy at times to the point of frustration 3) The "loose" crosshair for the automatic and silencer/pistols was just dumb and annoying when trying to be accurate with them
-Baffling lack of interactivity with objects in the levels hurt immersion - barely any objects except explosive barrels, etc. react when you shoot them
-Shallow story and very little characterization to the sniper you played or special enemies; considering how much time was spent on the level design, I feel like this game could have benefited from some optional collectible audio or diary tapes or classified documents that could have fleshed out the story and game world in a great way
Verdict: C+
Bottomline: I would only buy this game if it were on sale and you really love WW2-themed games and/or sniping. While the all out sniping sections of the game and the kill cam were very fun, the stealthier sections were way too numerous and felt ultra tedious.  After a couple missions into the single player campaign, I found myself going gung ho during almost all of the stealth sections and using cheap tactics to take out enemies as fast as possible even if meant dying and restarting a checkpoint a couple times. In short, I hurried through levels to get to the more fun all out sniping sections of them.

I played through the game in one afternoon...I just couldn't stop! The only thing I wish is that it would have been longer, to be honest. The visuals were stunning, bold and subtle by turns - I found myself especially appreciating the little details like how the snow blows differently as a visual cue right before a strong wind. There were a couple of places where I wasn't sure what to do (or just couldn't get it the first few times; I'm not that great at platformers) and got a little frustrated, but there's no real penalty for messing up and the mechanics are so fun and the game so engrossing that even having to redo the same sequence a couple of times didn't really draw me out of it. The narration was wonderful, and although I'm not usually interested in watching videos, I was actively searching levels to find and unlock new clips in this game! It was fascinating to learn so much about a culture I've never really been exposed to, to hear their music and stories and beliefs. I would be delighted for a sequel or anything else like this, I really really enjoyed it. I played single-player, which was a little rough at times, switching back and forth too slowly got me killed a couple of times, so I'd love to give this a try with a friend!

Waking Mars is a good Metroidvania type of game. Well, that's not entirely true. You won't be using guns and you won't upgrade any gear except for your jetpack. But the level design plays like any of them anyway, and unlike the Metroidvania games it's actually split up in smaller levels instead of offering one giant world. I'm not even sure if the comparison is now justified anymore... Anyway, moving on.
You've landed on Mars and your job is to discover the mysteries of the ecosystem when you become trapped in this huge cave. So you'll be picking up seeds and plant them in order to create life. Blue seeds go into the blue soil, green into the green soil, et cetera. Sounds fun, right ? It does. For a couple of hours, at least. Then it starts to feel repetitive, and it even manages to become frustrating, especially when you want to 5-star every level and your plants are eating or killing other forms of life around you, decreasing your rating.
Other than creating life there are a few mini-games in the game to spice things up and to get the story going but it's nothing noteworthy to begin with.
I do have to praise the developer for creating such colorful and sharp art. It looks great, but animating the cutscenes a little more would've been a good idea I think. Those parts are just too static.
Soooo.... let's see. I have no idea why I finished the game in the first place so I guess it must've done something right in the end... ? I'm not sure. Check the game out and decide for yourself.

As I believe someone else said, I wish there was a thumb going sideways.. a more neutral response.
The Bad:
This game is a lot shorter than any other games of similar genres that I have played. Like, way way too short (especially for the 14.99 price tag)... it only took me 2 hours to play through it the first time, and that's with actually reading everything. It only lasts the Summer (which I think had been a period of 4 months). Most games of this type tend to be at least a year.. So I didn't feel that you had a lot of time to make the choices you need.
You also only get to decide on one thing to do every day. In the morning you work in your little garden patch, and then in the afternoon you do the one thing you decided to do (Eg. Go to the library, or for a run).
Far too often spending time with the girls is nothing more than a filler "It was a lot easier to run with Clara today than usual... and so another day is over". It's a little annoying to find out that you wasted your only choice that day by getting nothing but filler text.
When you do have a "meaningful" interaction with someone, you only get to choose one response through the whole thing (more often than not) and everything else is pre-determined.. so I found that the character did/said far too many things that I wouldn't have done, had I been given the option. More often than not♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off people that you didn't intend to anger.
I also, personally, found that choosing any of the women was quite limiting, as Steve makes it very clear that he still wants to be with his ex-girlfriend Jill... there by making chasing any of the other women just seem weird.... and when I did finally decide I like one of the other girls, I was able to get my relationship to the highest it could be... and we just ended up being friends.. not really sure what happened there.
The good:
The farming is decent, it doesn't make the game, but it doesn't break it either.
The characters are decently interesting, if you ever actually get the time to talk to them in a capacity other than the flavour text added in the game, and the writing is fairly good.
The music isn't bad, I had my volume down, so I didn't pay too much attention to it.
The art is quite nice.
All in all, I would give this game 50%.. it isn't good, but it isn't bad either... however, it's not worth 15 dollars.. so if you can get it on sale, then it's worth it, but you shouldn't buy it at full price.

The farming really doesn't add too much to the game, just feels like a distracting mini-game in this dating sim. The pests and weeding make it slightly less boring and alright. The story itself seems alright, you get sent to your uncle's house for the summer for having bad grades, breaking up with Jill, and having a generally lazy attitude. Over time, you get better at gardening (or just don't bother at all and watch the wees grow, best thing EVER!), and can try to get with one of the four ladies. Kind of odd you have a Relationship bar with your uncle....
Getting the endings can be a bit stressful since even if you do max out the relationship bar and continue to visit with the ladies, there is a chance they will never date you or have an ending with you which means having to either restart from the earliest checkpoint (save right after getting to Sam's house is recommended) or starting all over again from the start. The music fits a lot of the places and sadly the music seems to be the only thing I enjoyed about the game in the end.
While the game does have a few good moments if done correctly, it's just a really bad mix of dating sim and tossing in farming for money to buy... well, nothing but more seeds really. You can get one of the ladies flowers much later in the game but that's just Susana being polite towards you.
