Feeling sad by writing this review but... After playing some old school shooters like Doom, Quake, Heretic and Hexen 1 itself, I cant recommend this game.
Presentation
The game itself looks and plays great. It runs in an altered Quake 1 engine and is fully 3d, unlike Hexen 1, which, just like Doom, uses 2d sprites for enemies and items. I have no ploblems running this game on my machine (win. 8). The environments and enemies bring a gothic and dark feeling, with great soundtrack that emphasises the overall grim atmosphere that the game has. Just like Hexen 1 you chose a few character classes that have different weapons and use the two types of mana in different ways. Its kind of an attempt to include RPG elements in a shooter.
Puzzles and Problems
Eventhough it looks and plays great, the reason why I dont recommend this game is that its virtually impossible to advance the game without some kind of guide or walkthrough. The shooting and killing is sporadic, and you will spend most of the time trying to solve hundreds of impossible puzzles, that require you to go to a certain location, pick up a hidden item, then teleport to another location, pull that lever... Its not a shooter like Quake, the devs pick up the simple puzzles from Hexen 1 and created something really annoying, that requires you to be constantly looking for answers on the internet as you just cant figure out by yourself using exploration. If you want a good fast paced shooter like Duke Nukem, Quake and Heretic, this game is not for you.
Get Hexen 1, Heretic or Quake instead.

I got this as a part of the "Star Wars Humble Bundle" a while back and have only just got around to playing it back to back with its predecesor.  All in all, this is a mixed bag of bits.  If you have played the previous episode, disappointment will set in rather quickly.   Graphically, character animations are much improved from the original, but backgrounds seem to be standard fodder and there is a marked difference in quality of some levels.   Sound and effects are satisfying, and the game doesnt suffer the random volume levels of the previous one where background n arration and music would drop out for no reason.  Satisfying sound a-la Lucasfilm and Star Wars themes a plenty here.

Gameplay wise however the game falls flat on its face.  The game suffers from tedious poor story and level development, making you duplicate the levels backwards in places to act as filler.  Camera focus is annoying and often leads you to wish you could pull the camera back just to see what you are doing.  in other places, the system, works fine, so its not a complete waste, but it could have been better.  All in all, the level design is a bit dull.  This wouldnt be too bad if the general tone of the missions was different but monotonous repetitive grinding gets boring after a while.
Although theres are some nice touches (breakable environments, the occasional heroic cutscene as you destroy a big boss (a-la Gods Of War), and your force powers have a decent effect on the enemies and environments, the bad sides of the gameplay spoil what could have been a great game into a mediocre 3rd person lightsaber grind.
Story wise, this is pretty lame.  without giving too much away, theres one part that was completely un-necessary and was just there to get you from place a to place b.  theres no fluid action in this game.  its stop/start "kill enemies/watch cutscene of new enemies appearing/repeat".  crowbaring other canon characters into the game was stupid as well.  its smacks of desparation as the devs just didnt have any ideas and ended up snatching defeat from teh jaws of victory.  Frankly, if the devs havent learned how to write a decent game yet and are relying on the star wars name and licence to sell it, its no wonder it is held in such revile by fans of the Star Wars universe.
Recommended for fans of Star wars and people who are that bored that they need a short game to pass a few hours with some utterly ridiculous plot points, but this is lame in comparison to the original and youll porobably never play it again

If you're here for a review for this game, you should get out if here. If you want a review of minecraft, here it is.
Minecraft is a sandbox game with worlds that will go on forever. They will never end. Your imagination is unlimited. If you can think of it, you can do it- or find it online. You can also play in multiplayer servers whether it's survival or mini games.
SinglePlayer Portion of the Review
Minecraft single player is pretty good. You start off with nothing but your fists and your inventory. You start by creating wooden tools and use them to get more materials. Slowly, you start to build up your character and become overpowered. You use these tools to fight the 3 bosses: Elder Guardian, Wither, and Ender Dragon. The Elder Guardian and Wither will be difficult, but the Ender Dragon is another story. Even though Minecraft has no story or campaign, killing the Ender Dragon will end the game. When I say end the game, I mean finish the game. You can still work on things you were working on. After you beat the Ender Dragon, you beat the game. Although, you can attempt to respawn the Ender Dragon, and get some of your own pair of Elytra. After you have done this, you can try thinking of some projects to work on, but after you do quite a bit of them, you'll find that the game gets boring fast. I don't recommend making a new world either because it would feel so slow, because your previous worlds would feel fast. The worlds just get boring and singleplayer replayability is low. Till the mods hit you baby. The mods are just, AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAHHHHHHHHH. That's all i got to say about the mods man.
Multiplayer Portion
The multiplayer portion is a weird experimental portion of the game. People find IPs of servers online and log into them. Hypixel is definitely the best and most popular one. But you can still check out some others like MinePlex or the Hive, or some small ones. In these types of servers, you go on them to play mini games. Most of them are just PvP(Player Vs Player) based, which keeps people playing the game competitively. PrestonPlayz is  a good example of a competitive minecraft player. PvP isn't the only thing though. You can do things like Build Battle, Hide and Seek, etc. If you're bad at PvP, which you are, you are probably going to play these gamemodes more often. Your friends can also create their own server, which does take a 1GB of your RAM, you can make it private or public. They just have to get the IP to it. The owner of the server can make it into anything they want. It can be a cool SMP(Survival Multiplayer) or just a world where they experiment. If you also have a cool single player world that you want to show off, you can go to your friend's house and turn on that LAN button, which lets everyone in your Local Area Network to join! What fun! The Multiplayer portion is a very good portion of the game, which also leads people to comeback to this game to play for more.
There's more to the game, but I'm to lazy to review it. In conclusion: This game is a wonderful masterpiece. I give it a 9.6/10

Story
After a severe car accident, Simon Jarrett suffers from severe brain damage, searching for medical help he agrees to an undergo experimental procedure. Simon has an unexpected blackout during the procedure and wakes up inside PATHOS-II, an underwater station tucked deep below the Atlantic Ocean. With no idea how he ended up there, Simon searches for answers and a way to return to home. Encountering enemies, nuetral forces, and friendly assistance, Simon uncovers memories of the past and terrors for what the future may hold.
A story about purpose, identity, and human life, Soma is breath of fresh air in terms of storytelling.
Gameplay
I don't mean this to pose as a con (it's worth noting)  but the controls themselves are shallow in terms of interaction with the world around you (more on this later). Typically a click of the mouse or click-and-drag mechanics are the extent of your capabilities, with a few exceptions where picking up and throwing objects is useful. Player and object/enemy animations are satisfactory and realistic. The enemy forces you meet inside the stations and while roaming the ocean floor come across life-like, and while their behavior is rather dumb at times, they still pose a challenge in certain instances.
Accurately believable physics and player movement build a sense of immersion. Chapter length and atmospheric variety set a nice pace that is both haunting and beautiful through out.
Sound
Incredible. Soma has arguably some of the best sound effects I've heard in a game. Every action no matter how minor feels like it was given careful planning in regards to how it would sound. Large metal airlock doors, compartments de-pressurising, pulling a levers and accessing control panels, a strong current flowing through a tunnel, all masterfully created to build a fuller experience for the player. All accompanied with sincere and emotional dialogue that is as engaging as it is thought-provoking. The characters you meet feel alive through their emotion fueled ideas, pleas, and thoughts.
Graphics
Beautiful. Paired with just as wonderful audio, Soma's graphics exceeded my expectations and the attention to enviromental detail is remarkable. Every room and corridor contain visually pleasing detail and their structural design gives the impression that they may actually exist.
Lighting and visual effects are as masterfully crafted as they are unsettling. Leaving the confines of the stations and roaming the ocean floor is about as eerie as you would expect while still maintaining an atmospheric beauty that makes you want to explore. Hands down an incredible experience visually.
Replay Value
What took about nine hours to complete with few instances of dragging, I would argue that though their is certainly a lot to discover, but there's not much worth going back for. Soma provides a compelling story that is unique and thought-provoking, but at the end it conveys what it wants the player to see and understand and closes the curtains.
Wrapping Up
I personally wouldn't quite peg Soma as a horror to those looking for a good scare but it is certainly suspenseful and unnerving.  As previously mentioned the controls themselves and interactions with the world around are shallow in complexity, but the combination of story, sounds, and graphics provide a truly wonderful experience. Incredible game overall, a must play.

To free the world of Eidolon's bane,
To prove that I am the Ancient Champion's scion.
First step drenched in cold and fear,
Starts in the sleepy city of Blackmarsh,
Where high towers dark skies tear,
And the Tailor hides a secret most harsh,
There I shall find skull wizards,
Spreading waste without hesitation,
And even when I avoid spilling my innards,
The General, Famine, is preparing plans for my extinction.
Swept away, I land among the sacrificial slabs of Mazaera,
Readying for another battle with were-panthers,
Blood-soaked stars are pointing me to step into the dark era,
Where Death awaits, offering only painful druthers.
Two Generals now are crowned in dust,
As I appear in the forgotten temples of Thysis,
Sands of time to me are showing a gesture of trust,
To the past I run, to rid myself of weakness and inner crisis.
My weapons of righteousness pointed to the Mummy Lords,
And Wheels of Time primed to strike in my favor,
Perished evil's screams resonates as calming chords,
Another General, Pestilence, acts to be a false savior.
My travel leads me further to the unforgiving Academy of Septimus,
Where War is the first and the last word of philosophy,
Most dangerous warriors of darkness, led by Medusas,
Still fail to protect their General, War, and its fleeting sovereignty.
But to be played so harshly by the last General,
Travelling half the world while seeking the source of Chaos,
Only at the end I find that first land I've stepped in hides the Devil,
This time however Eidolon shall meet my just fury's embrace.
Now all evil resides as an ugly, old memory,
Fair folks, just as I, return to their abode,
Still a feeling of uneasiness and anticipation sometimes overwhelms me,
For I know that every year, at least once, this game I shall play and download.

A sequel to the original, obviously, but more than that Rock of Ages 2 is improved in all aspects over the original. From traversing a map instead of playing linearly to having more units and boulders to choose from, there isn't an aspect that hasn't been re-tooled.
If you haven't played the first, you take a boulder and roll it towards your enemy gates. A few bashes, and it collapses, allowing you to run over the enemy general. However, bashing the door (or having your boulder broken) requires your minions to build a new boulder. While you wait, you can fill your side of the battlefield with things like walls and ballista. Mix in multiplayer and a few boss fights and the game will keep you busy for at least 6 to 10 hours.
The game runs on Unreal and from what I can tell, an older version of it. That means any computer in the last 15 years should run it well. Because the art assets and sound files are all Monty Python-esque, so they're not going to be stressing your hardware but at higher settings the game still looks quite nice.
Well it's fun. If you're looking for an action packed puzzle or strategy game, you should absolutely try it out. If you're a little strapped for cash the first exists and is cheaper but I'd recommend just saving up and grabbing the sequel.

I played it first during the Closed Beta at the end of January... First impressions ranged from very bad to horrible, but after an hour or 2 I got the basics down and it started becoming fun. I was destroying people left and right, even made many people rage quit, same goes for the Open Beta.
I was really hyped in the anticipation. After it came out I played it as much as I could for about 2 and a half weeks, it was pretty good and really fun, the Peer to Peer and the "pay to win" aspect didn't bother me since I mostly did 1v1s and 2v2s, where those 2 aren't an issue at all.
The gameplay is really solid, but after those first 2 and a half weeks I hadn't felt the need to play the game at all, I didn't play it for over 2 weeks and finally after I did play it, I only had a couple of 1v1 matches which I won, but I decided to close the game...
I have lost absolutely all interest in this game, and Idk why, maybe it's the poor balancing, but then again I played the 2 characters that are considered the "top-tier meta". I wasn't loosing either, my W/L ratio is in the top 2% of all For Honor players, but alas, I just don't feel any interest in continuing to play the game.
The reason why I don't recommend the game is because for anyone who's looking to get into the game at this point in its lifespan, be warned that pretty much all the players who still play it are harcore players who have been playing the whole time and have mastered the combat completely, newbies will get their asses kicked like there's no tommorow. That is mostly attributed to the fact that the game simply doesn't explain the more intricate parts of the combat, so newer players will easily get discouraged after a few hours of only taking Ls
Honestly, for what the game offers, 60€ is simply too much, and it is a really good game, it's just that Ubisoft found a way to ruin it...
